# Roadmap

Work top-to-bottom; `/dev-cycle` picks the first unchecked item. Check items off as they land (with tests). Keep milestones honest — an item isn't done until it works in the running app **and** over the control protocol.

> ## ⭐⭐⭐ CURRENT WORK ORDER — READ BEFORE PICKING AN ITEM. THIS OVERRIDES "top-to-bottom".

> **Take items from `## M39` FIRST, then `## M25`, then `## M24`. Do NOT default into M23.**

Order: a → b → c (correctness; independent of each other) → d → e (features) → f (spike) → g → h → i (debt/docs). Audit takeaway worth pinning: "the biggest wins were things the wire already did that no human could reach, and the worst bugs were on the newest and the oldest seams, not the middle."

## M14 — Gapless loop wrap (seeded 2026-07-12 from the m13-f design spike: docs/research/design-m13f-gapless-loop.md, GO-WITH-CONDITIONS; implementation follows that doc's §9 phases L-1…L-4 and §10 conditions C1–C8 verbatim — deviations return to the design doc for amendment)

**Standing law (C1)**: `GaplessLoopSpikeTests` (the L-0 splice-primitive pins, 4 tests) stays green forever; any splice regression blocks M14 work that day and converts the milestone to NO-GO/park with the spike retained as evidence (m10-p precedent). **Standing law (C4)**: zero new RT surface beyond the bounded cursor re-seek — no allocation, locks, or ObjC on the render path in ANY phase; any deviation returns to the design doc for amendment. Offline/render parity (§7): nothing changes offline, ever — provably (C8).

- [x] (m14-a / L-1) **Transport core** — AudioEngine + PlaybackGraph, control thread only: loop window in `scheduleAll`, per-cycle unrolled audio segments + baked-buffer cache, `derivedBeats` modular branch + timeline law, playhead-task top-up (`scheduledThroughCycle`), the wrap path stops calling `restart` (the graph never stops at wrap). Route: audio-dsp-engineer (design §2, §4 Option A, §8 failure modes 2–4). GATES: C1 spike suite green; C3 cycle-placement exactness — ≥3 unrolled cycles under a MULTI-SEGMENT tempo map, every audio anchor frame == the absolute integral with == pins (m12-c discipline; any `previous + loopFrames` accumulation found in review is a defect); C6 horizon law — schedule-ahead ≥ 2 playhead-tick periods, a 0.25-beat loop at 400 BPM sustains N ≥ 20 cycles with no starvation gap; C8 offline null-case — a non-looping project renders byte-identical (SHA) before/after, stems/bounce gates (Σ ≤ 1e-4, byte-identity) unaffected; C4. — **COMPLETE 2026-07-12, ALL GATES PASS + ONE MEASURED DESIGN AMENDMENT** (audio-dsp-engineer; orchestrator re-ran the suite, re-derived the C3 integral arithmetic by hand — cycle 108 000 frames, all 8 anchors exact — and mtime-proved wire untouched). Production surface = exactly 2 files (PlaybackGraph.swift, AudioEngine.swift) + GaplessLoopTransportTests(6). Mechanism per design names: `LoopWindow` in scheduleAll (:1632/:1697, nil = byte-identical linear path), `buildLoopUnroll`/`buildCyclePlan`/`enqueueLoopCycle` (anchors = absolute integral, never previous+loopFrames), baked fade/envelope pieces cached ONCE and re-enqueued per cycle, `beat(forElapsedSeconds:)` modular branch + `LoopContext` integrals, `serviceLoop` 33 ms top-up → `topUpLoopCycles` with `scheduledThroughCycle`; restart survives ONLY for loop edits/enable-mid-play (one seam, then gapless). **THE AMENDMENT (design §4-A + §8 modes 8–9, doc updated)**: "wrap-minus-margin" pre-queue is measured-UNSAFE — (8) drained-queue freeze: a strip-chain player whose queue fully drains never sounds later-queued items at ANY lead (33 696 frames still silent; bare player→mainMixer does NOT reproduce it, which is how L-0 missed it); (9) mid-flight splice needs ≥ ~2.5k frames of lead (item lost ≤2048, partial ~2300, clean ≥2496; L-0's 2928 margin sat just above the cliff). Remedy inside Option A: eager top-up ≥ max(horizon, sounding+2). EVIDENCE: C8 SHA `3c2adb8c…` before == after (4-track faded/enveloped/cross-rate/MIDI project, 2-segment map); C3 `cyclePlacementExactness` map 120→96@4→150@8 loop [2,6) — 150 never leaks (timeline law), 8/8 anchors ==; C6 `shortLoopHorizonLaw` 0.25-beat @ 400 BPM, 1800-frame cycles, 25 cycles at the 2-tick law minimum, 0 zero-frames + `horizonConstantHoldsTheLaw` pins production 0.2 s ≥ 2·33 ms; `wrapSpliceContinuity` 3 cycles 0 mismatches/0 zero-runs/0 sentinel leaks both seams bit-exact (old seam: 2880 silence + 1680 overshoot per wrap); `bakedPieceCycleReuse` cycles 1–2 bit-identical to head. INTERIM non-audio wrap (blessed C2-fallback, per-boundary via `wrapNonAudioSchedules` anchored on the TRUE boundary integral): MIDI flush+rebuild from loopStart (voices cut at wrap, ≤33 ms event ride-along/overshoot — today's class, no drift), automation republished (steps within a tick), metronome player-local re-anchor (boundary click may skip one cycle; <~100 ms loops jitter-class) — ALL replaced by L-2/L-3; recording keeps loop-suppression bit-identical. FLAKE (honest): one run's live-smoke wrap-count undercounted under parallel-suite starvation (5 pushes/1.7 s vs 44 isolated) — hardened to wraps ≥ 1, offline gates carry continuity. L-2 notes: replace wrapNonAudioSchedules+nonAudioLoopCycle with append-only unroll; lead thresholds do NOT apply to InstrumentSourceNode; loop-bounds DRAG = restart per edit → defer-to-drag-end noted for L-4/UX. 2150/249, wire 120/123 held.

## M15 — Post-gapless correctness & agent-ergonomics round (seeded 2026-07-13 from the post-M14 audit: docs/research/audit-m15.md, 12 findings F1–F12, 2 measured live bugs; orchestrator spot-checked the F1 both-call-sites citation, the F8 dismissal evidence, and the F5 mechanism before authoring) — **MILESTONE COMPLETE 2026-07-13 (a–g all verified)**

- [x] (m15-a) **Metronome meter-map correctness — the audit's HIGH measured bug (F1).** The live click ignores meter changes: with 4/4→3/4 at beat 8, downbeats land at 0,4,8,12,16,20 (constant 4/4) instead of 0,4,8,11,14,17,20 — measured via debug.masterCapture amplitude+frequency classification of all 23 clicks. Mechanism: `AudioEngine.clickMeterMap` builds `MeterMap(constant:)` from the cached `beatsPerBar` scalar (AudioEngine.swift:1607-1609; cache :1478) — and `OfflineRenderer.swift:246` does the SAME (its in-code claim "offline callers pass real maps" is FALSE — only tests pass real maps); count-in inherits the scalar too (wrong bar length in a non-base meter, code-proven). Fix: plumb the REAL `store.transport.meterMap` through both call sites + count-in; the Metronome API is already fully MeterMap-aware (m14-c) so this is plumbing, S-sized, control-plane only. Route: audio-dsp-engineer. GATE: the audit's capture probe re-run verbatim — live 4/4→3/4 downbeats at 0,4,8,11,14,17,20 by amplitude+frequency classification; offline render click positions == the meter map; count-in bar length correct in 3/4; C8-style null era (constant-meter project byte-identical); the m14-c meter pin extended to the LIVE path. — **COMPLETE 2026-07-13, ALL GATES PASS** (audio-dsp-engineer). Production surface = 4 files. AudioEngine.swift: the cached `beatsPerBar` scalar is GONE from the engine (it existed solely for the click map + count-in) — `cacheTransportFlags` caches the WHOLE `transport.meterMap` as the stored `clickMeterMap` (a trivial project synthesizes the constant map, so the null case is arithmetic-identical), the computed constant-map property and its false comment DELETED, all four live schedule sites read the cache, count-in derives bar length from it. Metronome.swift: `countInPlan`/`scheduleCountIn` take `meterMap:` — bar length = the meter AT THE RECORD BEAT (the m12-b tempo LOOKUP policy's meter twin: count-in precedes the record beat in wall time, the beat domain does not extend backward) + `receivedMeterMap` test seam. OfflineRenderer.swift: `render(beatsPerBar:)` → `render(meterMap:)` (default trivial 4/4). ProjectStore.swift — **DISCOVERY: a meter-ONLY map change never reached the engine at all** (`applyTempoMap` pushed only on tempo change; `restoreEditState` likewise), which would have left the new cache stale mid-play: both funnels now push the click-player-local `metronomeChanged` intent on a meter-only change (transport/clip players untouched; tempo changes need nothing extra — setTempo's restart re-caches + reschedules); stale "meter needs no engine push" comments corrected. EVIDENCE — the audit probe VERBATIM (headless staging :17641, project.new → `tempo.setMap {segments, meterChanges}` → setMetronome → debug.masterCapture 552 000 frames): 23/23 clicks classified by amplitude AND frequency, zero ambiguity — downbeats 0,4,8,11,14,17,20 EXACT (0.483 @ 1609 Hz vs 0.333 @ 1000 Hz); the bug pattern 0,4,8,12,16,20 dead; app killed by exact pid, port verified closed, .ips listings byte-equal. PROBE QUIRK for the next agent: `debug.masterCapture start` REQUIRES a running engine — warm-up play/stop first (`stopPlayback` leaves the hardware engine running). OFFLINE == MAP: the same scenario through OfflineRenderer, all 23 clicks classified, downbeats == the map — the m14-c meter pin now covers the offline PATH, not just the API. COUNT-IN: unit pins (constant 3/4 ⇒ 3 clicks; audit map ⇒ 3 at beat 9, 4 at beat 0, 3 at beat 8 — right-continuous) + a rendered `scheduleCountIn` pin (2 bars at beat 9 ⇒ 6 clicks, downbeats on clicks 0/3, silence after). PLUMBING CHAIN pinned at both links: intents cache `transport.meterMap` ITSELF (headless pin) + live smoke — all FOUR live schedule paths hand the Metronome the real 2-change map verbatim. NULL ERA: new permanent 4/4-only anchor pair OFF `a3927faf…` / ON `7dd272aa…` byte-identical before/after the change (the OFF SHA coincides with the m14-c fixture's because that fixture's 120→90 boundary sits past all its clip content — noted in the suite header); the m14-c era pair OFF `a3927faf…` / ON `692e713d…` HELD through the only test call-shape changes (`beatsPerBar: 3` → the equivalent constant map, 3 sites, zero expectation changes). 2168/253 → **2173/254** (+5 tests, +1 suite MetronomeMeterMapTests), npm 86/86, wire **120/123 HELD** (DAWControl/mcp-server mtimes pre-date the session), build warning-clean, C4 zero new RT surface (control-thread scheduling only).
- [x] (m15-b) **Loop-cycle take recording (M5 iii-b — the M14 dividend) + record×loop honesty (audit F2).** Live-proven dishonesty today: record with loop [0,4) enabled starts at the playhead (17.096) and rolls LINEAR while the snapshot still reports `isLoopEnabled: true` — the suppression is silent. Design note FIRST (short, in-repo: record-seeks-to-loop-start semantics, cycle boundaries = new take lanes on the SAME take group, the two suppression sites from design-m13f §6.1 lifted together — `startPlayers(scheduleLoop: false)` + the playhead `activeTake == nil` guard; count-in stepper rider from the audit). Then implement: each loop pass lands a new lane (the m10-era take-lane machinery is the landing surface), stop finalizes the last partial cycle honestly. Route: daw-architect design note → audio-dsp-engineer (engine) with store-side landing per the note. GATE: offline-driven loop-record of ≥ 3 cycles → 3 take lanes with cycle-exact boundaries (== integrals); mid-cycle stop → honest partial lane; non-loop recording byte-identical (era); wire `transport.record` semantics documented — if a behavior flag is needed it must NOT grow the wire count silently (teaching error or param on the existing verb, decided in the design note); the B2 dishonesty dead: record+loop either loops-and-lands-takes or REFUSES with a teaching error (no silent linear roll). — **COMPLETE 2026-07-13, ALL GATES PASS per design-m15b-loop-record §11 G1–G10** (audio-dsp-engineer). Caught by the agent reading §6 more carefully than I had; verified firsthand with a standalone `edgecheck.swift` before accepting it.** The fix makes mixer→outputNode EXPLICIT at 48 k, and the topology read-back (`mixer out 48000 / outputNode in 48000 / outputNode out 44100`) is a PER-RUN PRECONDITION THAT FAILS THE RUN — a discarded `connect()` would silently reproduce the old graph and print a clean-looking result from a manipulation that never happened; confirmed on all 46 explicit-arm runs. **THAT MOVE IS ALSO THE CYCLE'S REAL MEASUREMENT: Δ(explicit − implicit) = `+0.948 / +0.935 ms`, so essentially the ENTIRE −0.94 ms belongs to the MIXER's SRC, not the output edge's.** **⚠️ AND THAT −0.94 ms IS NOT A COST ANYTHING PAYS TODAY — I MIS-STATED THIS TO THE USER AND IN THE CHANGELOG AS "the mixer, where it happens today"; CORRECTED 2026-07-31. Production converts NOWHERE: `AudioEngine.init`/`rebuildEngine` pass `graphRate: currentDeviceRate(of: engine)` (AudioEngine.swift:443/:980), so the live graph ADOPTS the device rate and no SRC exists in the steady state (exactly as m19-k's own record already said). The −0.94 ms is the price of building m20-d the NAIVE way — inject the project rate but leave mixer→outputNode implicit — so this probe is a BUILD INSTRUCTION for m20-d, not a defect report against the shipping app. m20-b found no bug; there is nothing here awaiting a fix.** **NUMBERS (N=5/leg, primary shape unless noted).** **P1** (48 k edge over 44.1 k device): 5/5, peak `996.991 Hz`, worst error `0.009 Hz` vs ±1 Hz — resample-by-relabeling would have read 1085.2 Hz. **⚠️ ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION, CAUGHT IN REVIEW AFTER THE FIRST TICK: the topology fix above was applied to `runAnchored` (P2X/P2X-A/P3X) but NOT to `runOnce`, so the P1 figure directly above was measured on `.implicitMixerSRC` — the very shape this record calls a trap four sentences earlier. The pitch-correctness CLAIM was never unsupported: P4's 44.1 k baseline segment is an explicit 48 k output edge over a 44.1 k device and reads the same `996.991 Hz`, and THAT is the output-edge correctness evidence. But the record had pinned the headline correctness leg to the wrong shape. GENERAL LESSON, and it is the same defect wearing a different hat: WHEN YOU FIX A TOPOLOGY/CONFIG BUG, ENUMERATE EVERY CALL SITE THAT BUILDS THAT THING — fixing the two legs whose numbers looked wrong left the leg whose number looked RIGHT still on the broken shape, and a correct-looking number is exactly what stops you re-checking. `runOnce` has since been given the same no-default `Topology` parameter and P1/P1-F re-run on `.explicitOutputEdge`; see the re-run line at the end of this record. **P2X** (explicit output edge + passthrough): constant `+0.025 ms`, spread `0.022 ms` vs one device quantum `11.610 ms` (512 frames); `lastRenderTime.sampleTime` mean slope `44101.0 Hz` — **1.0 Hz from the device rate, 3899.0 Hz from the project rate**, so the output edge is unambiguously in the DEVICE clock domain (B1/B2 paired). **P2X-A** (explicit, no effect): PASS, spread `0.012 ms`. **P3X**: `+0.004 ms` added latency. **P4** (44.1→48→96 k mid-play, restart WITHOUT reconnect): 10/10 flips, 15/15 rate points, worst pitch error `0.020 Hz`; edge input scope read 48 k before AND after every restart; `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` arrived 10/10. All of 44.1/48/96 k are supported (`AvailableNominalSampleRates` = 8k…768k), so the skip path never fired. **P5 — NOT RUN**: BlackHole 2ch is stereo-only and staging a mono/aggregate device would mean creating a system audio device; §6 marks P5 opportunistic and explicitly not gateable, so this is a recorded non-result, not a gap. **EVERY LEG HAS A FALSIFIABILITY SIBLING, because five byte-identical runs look the same as a probe printing a constant.** P1-F: same path at 440 Hz reads `439.993 Hz`. P3-F/P3X-F: a known 10.000 ms of injected leading silence is observed as `+10.004`/`+9.995 ms`. P4's capture-side control inverts into a proof — a capture asked for a 44.1 k client format over a 96 k device BUILDS AND STARTS CLEANLY and then delivers ZERO frames, so a flip that had not really taken would have starved the capture and produced a NIL pitch, never a wrong one. **A HYPOTHESIS OF MINE WAS FALSIFIED BY THE DATA AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE:** I predicted the implicit arm's NEGATIVE latency (`−0.94 ms`) was an artifact of the fixed `abs > 0.05` onset threshold tripping early on the converter's smeared edge, and briefed the agent to treat it that way. An energy-envelope estimator (50 %-of-plateau, ~5× less edge-sensitive) reproduced it to within `0.010 ms` at two window sizes. **It is a real property of the mixer-SRC graph's anchor-to-output mapping, not a detection bias — and the cautionary phrasing does not apply to the output-edge arm at all, whose figure is POSITIVE.** **OTHER FINDINGS WORTH CARRYING:** (a) **SDK, 10/10 flips — after a configuration change `engine.isRunning == false` while `player.isPlaying == true`; any recovery path gating on `player.isPlaying` gets a FALSE POSITIVE** (check against the real `recoverEngine` at Phase 2). (b) **At a 48 k device rate the "edge still reports 48 k" criterion is a CONSTANT FIELD and cannot discriminate** — "persisted" and "silently re-derived to the device rate" print the same number; read P4's 15/15 as **10 discriminating + 5 consistent-but-mute**. (c) The §6 passthrough is `AVAudioUnitEQ(numberOfBands: 0)`, proven unity rather than assumed — an offline null test gave worst `|out − in| = 0.000e+00` over 48000 frames and `latency = 0.0 s`; inserting it changed the constant by `−0.008/+0.010 ms`, i.e. nothing. **ENVIRONMENT HAZARDS, both real and both caught by instrumentation rather than by luck:** BlackHole **WEDGED once** — it accepted `AudioDeviceStart` (rc 0, `IsRunning`→1) and delivered **ZERO IOProc callbacks**, silence indistinguishable from a broken converter; triggered after an UNCATCHABLE ObjC exception (`player did not see an IO cycle`) killed the process mid-stream while it held the device started, which also bypassed the rate restore. Answered by `waitForIOCycle` (prevents the abort), `run.sh` (restores the rate from a signal trap, proven by aborting a stub), and `halcheck` (raw-HAL preflight; healthy ≈172 @44.1k / ≈188 @48k / ≈376 @96k, zero = wedged). Recovery is `sudo killall coreaudiod` — **the user's call, never the probe's.** Second hazard: a pass-1 P4 run failed when **the user's AirPods connected mid-run**, re-enumerating devices so AVAudioEngine's output AUHAL fell back to the new system default (`pinnedDev=197`, a device absent from the list); halcheck read 376 immediately after, so NOT a wedge. **The `pinnedDevice` read-back is exactly what turned that into a legible routing diagnosis instead of a converter fault.** **SAFETY, deliberate deviation from §6:** the design doc says to make BlackHole the DEFAULT OUTPUT; that would silence the user's speakers machine-wide, so both units are pinned at the AUHAL and **the system default was never read-modify-written**. The only device setting written anywhere is BlackHole's nominal rate — §6's named test surface — restored on every exit path (verified back at its 48000 entry rate). `ZoomAudioDevice`/`ParrotAudioPlugin`/built-ins never opened. **Routing note: done by `audio-dsp-engineer` across three delegations**, after the user corrected a standing misreading that had been keeping this work in the main context. **P1 RE-RUN ON `.explicitOutputEdge` (4th delegation, post-review — closes the attribution gap flagged above): `996.991 Hz` 5/5, worst error `0.009 Hz`; P1-F control `439.993 Hz` with the 997 Hz criterion NOT met, as required. BYTE-IDENTICAL to the implicit figures — `frames`/`peak`/`rms` too.** ⚠️ **AND IDENTITY HERE IS THE EXPECTED RESULT, NOT A FINDING, WHICH IS WHY IT MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE: a mixer at unity with a single input is a passthrough, so both topologies hand the SAME converter the SAME 48 k sine; and P1 could not have resolved a difference regardless — the 65536-point FFT at 44100 Hz has a `0.672913 Hz` bin and the 0.009 Hz error is ~1/75 of one. **THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE THE TWO TOPOLOGIES ARE EQUIVALENT** — P2X-A/P3X carry that question and their answer is the opposite (`+0.948 ms`).** What DOES prove the graph actually changed is a positive printed discrimination, pre-registered from the prior log before re-running: the per-run topology read-back triple, which reads `mixerOut=44100 edgeIn=44100 edgeOut=44100` on the implicit arm and `48000/48000/44100` on the explicit one — **verified firsthand across both logs, not taken from the agent's report** (9 implicit / 13 explicit triples in the old log; all 5 new P1 runs explicit). A same-number result with no such discriminator would have been indistinguishable from an edit that never took effect. **THE AGENT THEN FOUND A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE VERY BUG IT WAS SENT TO FIX** — the summary block still grouped P1 under an `IMPLICIT topology` heading, so the next default full-ladder run would have printed a true P1 PASS under a false topology label; fixed, along with two stale comments asserting `runOnce` leaves the output edge implicit. That is the enumerate-every-call-site lesson recurring inside its own repair. **TWO CARRY-FORWARD CAVEATS.** (1) My brief asserted a leg-selection mechanism existed; it did not — `m20b` ignores argv entirely, so `M20B_ONLY_P1` is a NEW knob, not a discovered one (early-exit sited after P1-F; the default unset run is still the full ladder). (2) To avoid a divergent second copy, `connectEdges`/`topologyReadBack` were extracted from `runAnchored` and shared with `runOnce` — **so the published P2/P3/P2X/P3X numbers were taken on the PRE-refactor tree and P2 was NOT re-run against the post-refactor one.** **THE RECORDED CONSTANTS ARE UNAFFECTED, AND THAT — NOT THE PROBE'S DISPOSABILITY — IS WHY NO RE-RUN WAS OWED: they are measurements of code that actually ran, and a refactor applied afterwards cannot retroactively change what a completed measurement read.** The extraction being mechanical, and the probe being scratchpad-only (never shipped; m20-d's gate is the live app, not this probe), is only why it was not worth another device-touching pass for the SEPARATE question of whether the probe still reproduces them. So: the constants above stand as written and are not stale — but a future re-run that disagrees with them should suspect THIS refactor first, not measurement flake.

The agent then measured WHICH action storms: flip alone → 0 in both arms; **parameter-only mutation (`track.setVolume`) → 0 real / 41 mutant, THE STORM**; teardown-class mutation (add+remove track) → 0 in both, because by then the mutant has already re-keyed. **A gate that used only the teardown-class change — the obvious design, and the one m20-d used — would have read ZERO re-prepares in the mutant and gone confidently hollow.** The param-only mutation is the trigger precisely because it is the FIRST `tracksDidChange` after the flip.
  **THE SEAM (no new wire surface):** `note.audition`'s `reason` field. `auditionAudibility` (`AudioEngine.swift:1313`, read firsthand) checks `auRegistry.preparedInstrument(forTrack:) == nil` synchronously and returns `.inaudibleNotReady` — the registry's own prepared state on an existing verb. ⚠️ It is PRIORITY-ORDERED behind mute/solo, `!isRunning` and `noRenderer`, so a single sample can be masked; the legs therefore ask "did `instrumentNotReady` EVER appear in this window", never "what was the reason at time T".

On the real tree that leg is deterministically green — a constant rate cannot move whenever the rebuild lands, which is m20-d's whole point.** Storm COUNTS vary run to run (the hammer samples a millisecond-scale window); what reproduced exactly across both mutant runs is the SET of legs that redden, minus that race.
  **⚠️ THE FINAL-STATE TRAP, worth carrying to any future rate gate: at the END of the run the MUTANT reads 48000 too**, because its last rebuild happened with the device back at 48 kHz. - [x] (m23-a) **Mixer strip layout: the m22-e insert-chip REGRESSION, plus panel collapse + a volume knob.** User report: "in Mix tab when it adds inserts and other instruments or effects it eclipses the volume scales." m22-e is what ADDED insert chips with five-cell activity bars, and the tested bundle contains it — treat as a shipped-quality regression and fix FIRST. Three parts: (1) the strip must reserve the fader/scale region so inserts can never overlap it (`Sources/DAWApp/Mixer/MixerStripView.swift`, 37.7 KB — the layout owner); (2) a collapsible instrument/insert top panel so manual fader work always has room; (3) a round VolumeKnob beside the existing `PanKnob` (`MixerControls.swift:99` is the precedent to mirror — same idiom, no new mechanism). Pure-view work: wire/MCP delta ZERO. Route: ui-design-engineer. GATE: staging captures at both densities with a full insert chain proving no overlap, Simple/Pro flip, suites. — **DONE 2026-07-26 (ui-design-engineer).** Root cause was one line: the fader's hard `.frame(minHeight: 150)`. A hard minimum is exported UP to a console that has no vertical scroll, so a growing chain made the whole mixer demand more height than the window had. **Blast radius was wider than the report:** at 760 pt the app header row AND transport bar were pushed clean off-window before any strip clipped; at 640 the strip clipped BOTH ends (an over-tall `VStack` centres and spills both ways — track name at the top, dB + Mute/Solo/Arm at the bottom). The master strip was a SEPARATE contributor with its own larger minimum; fixing channels alone would have left it. FIX: `MixerStripLayout` (new, headless `DAWAppKit`) splits a strip into a RESERVED cluster that never yields (header · VOL|PAN · fader+meter+dB · Mute/Solo/Arm) and exactly ONE yielding region (the Pro signal-flow block). `signalFlowRoom(available) = max(0, min(available*0.55, available − reserved))` — **content-independent, which is why it holds at any chain length**. The region is a bounded `ScrollView(.vertical).frame(maxHeight: room).fixedSize(vertical: true)`: `fixedSize` is load-bearing (a ScrollView's ideal height is its content's, so the region becomes inflexible at `min(content, room)` and the greedy fader absorbs the rest). Implementer REPLACED its own first cut — `ViewThatFits + maxHeight + layoutPriority(1)` passed the letter of its gate but left a 2-insert strip holding a ~200 pt void with the fader crammed at the bottom (a `maxHeight` frame stretches to whatever it is proposed): **the guard rail was reintroducing the failure it exists to remove.** Collapse disclosure PERSISTS as `panelLayout.mixerInsertsCollapsed` (console-wide, app-sticky, default EXPANDED so chains don't vanish on update; a disclosure, not a density mode → no chip; inventory verdict at simple-pro-inventory.md:216). `VolumeKnob` additive (`VerticalFader` untouched), Canvas contract honoured, new shared `KnobGeometry` is now the ONE knob-path home with `PanKnob` refactored onto it; cyan not neutral (volume HAS a meaning-color: fader fill, dB readout, VOLUME automation lane), unipolar from range-min with a unity detent so it cannot disagree with the fader about 0 dB. Explain 88→**89**. DELIBERATE, DISCLOSED DEVIATION — Simple mode DID change (knob row 38→52 pt + the knob; pan readout moved inline to `PAN L64`, a change driven purely by the Pro budget): **ORCH ACCEPTED** — the brief's "Simple must not change" was protecting against REGRESSION, and Simple's regression behaviour is verifiably unchanged (Pro sections still hide whole, freed space still flows to the fader); one row anatomy beats two forked ones, and the knob belongs in Simple most of all. - [x] (m23-b) **Piano-roll keys read as gray because they ARE gray — make them piano.** Verified root cause: `Theme.swift:15-16` sets `keyBlack = 0x11141C` and `keyWhite = 0x2C3242` — BOTH dark, so the "white" keys render dark slate. The user is right and the fix is small. Retone `keyWhite` to a readable ivory and re-balance the grid lane stripes (`PianoRollView.swift:934`) so the black/white alternation reads at a glance without breaking the dark-glass language or note-block contrast. Route: ui-design-engineer. GATE: capture at both densities, note blocks still legible over both lane tones, DESIGN-LANGUAGE compliance note, suites. — **DONE 2026-07-26 (ui-design-engineer).** The roadmap framed this as a retone; it is really an **INK-INVERSION** item, and the naive one-hex change ships a broken gutter. `keyBlack`/`keyWhite` have ONE call site (`KeyboardSidebar.swift:36`) but FOUR house-chrome elements composite on top of the white rows, all light-on-dark by construction — `hairline` separator, `gridEmphasis` octave marker, `textDim` label, `playback` cyan middle C — measuring **1.02/1.05/2.19/1.07:1** on ivory, i.e. invisible. The labels are not an edge case: they draw at `pitch % 12 == 0` and **C is always a white key**. Continuous costs 65x the scroll traffic and **3.3x the main-actor latency** — 49 ms against a ~33 ms transport tick means the main actor is already behind the cadence it is following (the sampler getting 119 replies vs 100 in the same wall-clock window is the same fact from the other side). **The decisive column is `contentWidthChanges: 0` in BOTH**, which is what answers the delegation's stated worry directly: the marker WOULD re-lay-out scroll content per tick, except every target is clamped to `contentWidth - viewport`, which makes the lanes' `totalBeats` zoom padding (`availableWidth + max(0, hScrollApplyTarget)`) a no-op for follow. - [x] (m23-d) **Note audition: hear the pitch while you drag it.** Standard in every note editor and absent here (no audition/preview path in the piano roll — the `audition` hits in `AudioEngine.swift` are m22-g's reference lane, unrelated). Dragging a note vertically, and clicking a key in the sidebar, should sound the pitch on the track's instrument. Needs an engine seam to trigger a one-shot note outside the sequencer schedule, RT-safe and independent of transport state. Route: design pass by daw-architect on the trigger seam (must not perturb the render graph or the scheduled MIDI path), then audio-dsp-engineer. Triple required if a wire command is added (`note.audition` or similar) so the copilot can audition too. GATE: audible one-shot with transport stopped AND during playback without disturbing scheduled notes, no allocation on the render thread, suites. — **DONE 2026-07-26 (audio-dsp-engineer), built to `docs/research/design-note-audition.md`.** Five layers: a SECOND per-renderer `LiveEventRing` (`auditionRing`, cap 64, main actor = the single producer — made a type property by `@MainActor pushAudition`/`beatAuditionHeartbeat` rather than the doc's raw `.push` at the call site); `AuditionOutcome` + `setAuditionPitches`/`stopAllAudition` on `AudioEngineControlling` with protocol-extension defaults so the ~6 test fakes compile untouched; a `@MainActor AuditionController` in DAWCore (8-voice cap, 500 ms heartbeat, 30 s hold ceiling, last-call-wins one-shot); the wire triple `note.audition`; and the piano-roll drag + gutter press behind a debug-tier defeat switch (`debug.panelLayout {auditionEnabled}`, zero wire growth — the wire verb deliberately ignores it). **Liveness is a WATCHDOG, not a duration cap**: the renderer counts its own `renderedFrames` and cuts audition voices after 3 s without a heartbeat, so a crashed or wedged UI can never leave a note stuck, and no clock is ever read on the render thread. **DEVIATION FOUND AND AMENDED, not coded around (§6.3 → AMENDMENT A1):** the design's safety-release loop was unbounded, so on a dense-schedule quantum it wrote PAST the end of the preallocated merge buffer — reproduced first as `11 events out of an 8-slot buffer` (72 bytes past a 192-byte allocation) on the render thread, then closed with a computed `liveBlockBound` and a one-quantum DEFERRAL (6a does not clear the pitch map until the off is actually written, so the next quantum re-emits it — late, never lost). No capacity changed. Two smaller findings reported rather than built: §11.2's `soloExcluded` reason is unreachable given §7.1's merged `inaudibleMuted`, and §8.2's "reproduce the pitch↔y affine inline" was unnecessary (`PianoRollModel.pitch(forY:)` already exists; m16-a's `@Sendable` Canvas constraint binds the DRAWING closure, not a main-actor gesture handler). A hole the design did not cover was found at review and closed: `record()` now releases any HELD audition, because refusing new ones does nothing about a voice already sounding when the take starts — the heartbeat re-asserts it every 500 ms straight through the take and the capture ring cannot see it, so it would be heard and not recorded. **C18 staging gate 20/20** (`scripts/gates/m23d-note-audition.mjs`, port 17695, killed pidfile-exact): asserts AUDIO off `mixer.masterAnalysis`, never an ok response — transport STOPPED −80.00 dB floor → **−10.58 dB** sounding (+69.4) and back to the floor on release; DURING PLAYBACK the audition adds **+7.82 dB** over the running mix while the scheduled notes never fall below −14.44 dB, and after it releases the bus returns to within **0.98 dB** of the scheduled-only level (an `instrument.reset()`/`requestFlush()` would have collapsed it to −80 — that number IS the §5.3 proof); the debug switch OFF still sounds over the wire. Two gate-fixture defects were found and fixed by measurement, not by loosening a threshold: GM program 0 is a DECAYING patch, so both release legs were reading an envelope rather than the code (moved to the sustaining program 16), and "released" cannot be a single absolute dB — a note-off is followed by a release+reverb tail, so the gate samples twice 3 s apart and asserts the SHAPE (collapse −47.15 dB, then −57.73 → −80.00 = decaying tail, where a stuck voice would sit flat). §16 Q1 answered empirically: the first audition after `track.setInstrument` on a cold app answers `audible:false reason:"instrumentNotReady"` and becomes audible after **~250 ms** — `prepare()` from `setAuditionPitches` is necessary but the hosted instrument's async preparation is the real gate. C15 argued structurally line-by-line AND backstopped empirically: `malloc_zone_statistics` `blocks_in_use` delta **0** across 10 000 audition-carrying quanta, 4 runs (one-off probe, not left in the suite). 51 new tests / 5 new suites; Swift **3453/370** 0-warn (4 of 5 full runs fully green; the 5th hit only the known pre-existing `SoundBankHostingTests` T1 AU-preparation flake, which isolates 7/7 in 0.626 s), npm **212/212**; wire 152→**153** commands, 155→**156** router cases, MCP 155→**156** tools, Copilot catalog 65→**66**; both wire files' diffs are purely additive (`Commands.swift` +70/−0; `server.ts` +73/−1, the single deletion being the pre-existing uncommitted m22-g Opus-5 string). **REBUILD REQUIRED — `dist/DAWPro.app` predates this.** **ORCH VERIFICATION 2026-07-26 — TICK HELD (unticked by the orchestrator; the implementer had ticked it). Suites and wire are clean, but the FEATURE misbehaves audibly, so the box cannot stand.** Reproduced independently: Swift **3453/370** 0-warn fully green (the AU flake did not fire on the orch run), npm **212/212**, wire pins 153/156/66 with `note_audition` the only new MCP tool and the sole `server.ts` deletion the pre-existing m22-g Opus-5 string — additive-only holds. **C13 PASSED and is now measured rather than argued**: rendering the same project with a live audition sounding produced a BIT-IDENTICAL file (`eb006812a9338a36…`, 1156096 bytes both), so a held audition can never reach an export. **The defect: the audition note is released immediately instead of held, and a SECOND note sounds at t≈`durationMs`.** The control that makes it airtight is internal to one session on the built-in polySynth — a SCHEDULED 6-beat note holds FLAT at −14.5 dB for 6 s, while a `durationMs:4000` audition traces −12.9 → −77.7 over 4.1 s, which is the exact shape of that instrument's release envelope (measured separately with a 0.25 s scheduled note: −11.0 → −80 over ~4.5 s). Rises >8 dB occur ONLY at 0.15 s and 4.26 s, and the second tracks `durationMs` exactly (2.27 s for 2000, 4.26 s for 4000). **That >8 dB detector alone could NOT have exonerated the heartbeat** — a re-push of an already-open pitch lands on a voice already in release, so it would re-onset QUIETER than the previous peak and never trip an 8 dB rise; sampling at 150 ms cannot resolve a 500 ms sawtooth either.   flat sum with per-channel ripple `1 ± s`, while two different all-passes give flat channels and a
  COMBED sum. There is no third arrangement. **This kind always takes the flat mono sum** and reports
  the cost per instance as `channelPeakDb`/`channelNotchDb` rather than hiding it. Measured mono
  fold-down at width 1.8 / spread 0.8: level **−7.9e-10 dB**, worst band **−3.7e-9 dB**, residual
  **−145.8 dB**. The Haas control the item warned about, on the same instrument: **−10.257 dB** at
  440 Hz and a residual **+4.26 dB — LOUDER than dry**. The item's own stated failure, reproduced on
  demand.

  accidentally bit-exact, and (b) the ride value landed the accumulator on exactly 1.0 — only
  **99 of 1650** three-decimal widths in [0.3, 1.95] leave any residue at all. ⭐ **A fixture can be
  the reason a test cannot fail.** Fixed with an asymmetric fixture (L = 1e-7, R = 0.9) and a ride of

  in the side path PASSES the mono-compatibility oracle — any `S' = F(M)` is mono-safe, so a Haas
  trick hidden in the side channel would have cleared the item's own acceptance test. A separate leg
  measures impulse-response DISPERSION (745 samples above 1 % of peak, largest single sample 4.07 %
  of energy; a plain delay gives 1 sample / 100 %).

## M28 — The Breath Pad: a circular effort-morph controller for wind/bowed realism (seeded 2026-08-19 from the user's own idea — *"controller with big circular knob where the dot is moving between different patterns placed around the circle… we need to mimic human playing to the max"*)

**USER AUTHORISATION 2026-08-19**, verbatim: *"let's go with what architect suggest and what will provide the best and quality results"* — i.e. the FULL P1–P7 scope, not the P1+P2+P4 minimum. Design: `docs/research/design-breath-pad.md` (19 §§). Measurement: `docs/research/measure-gm-sax-cc.md`.

⛔⛔ **SHAPE RULED: build the WRITE-MODE pad (a). DECLINE the general engine modulation source (b).** Decisive reason, verified in source not assumed: `.soundBank` tracks are reachable ONLY as MIDI bytes (`HostedAUInstrument.swift:203` emits `0xB0`), so a per-block engine modulator would have to be re-quantised into CC events to reach the user's sax at all — arriving at (a) with extra steps. (b)'s one unique capability is wall-clock-varying modulation, which the user's own reproducibility requirement FORBIDS. (b) ≈ 15–20× leg D plus permanent RT surface; (a) ≈ 5–6×.

⭐⭐⭐ **THE PAD LAW — `effort(t)` IS A PURE FUNCTION OF (musical position, seed, path). NEVER wall-clock.** If the dot wanders on elapsed time, a bounce cannot match what was heard and every offline-render gate in this tree stops working. The seeded random walk must be position-pure fBm, **never an accumulator** — an integrator is deterministic-given-a-seed and passes the naive test, yet `extendLoopMIDI`'s per-cycle rebuild from `loop.startBeat` (`PlaybackGraph.swift:2923-2930`) would give cycle 5 a different path than cycle 1.

⭐⭐ **AIR BUDGET MUST BE LEGIBLE.** A phrase going quiet because the model decided the player ran out of air, with nothing saying so, is a silent override of composer intent — the same defect class as the seven inert CC11 lanes. **USER RULING 2026-08-19: `air.enforced` DEFAULTS TO `false`** with a prominent switch (the user answered "yes" to *should running out of air constrain the result* — a model-behaviour question — and separately accepted the architect's `false` default).

⚠️⚠️ **FOUR MEASURED FACTS (2026-08-19) THAT OVERRIDE THE PRE-MEASUREMENT DESIGN TEXT. Do not build from the older wording.**
1. ⛔ **On `.soundBank` (the user's sax) CC 11 moves NO filter — it is EXACTLY a gain**, MIDI square law `(v/127)²`, any non-gain difference bounded at **−104 dB**. Control fired (the same scalar fit REFUSES on the built-in sampler's real filter at −9.75 dB — 95 dB separation), so this is a measured negative, not a failed measurement. **The pad on a sound-bank track is a loudness-and-pitch device. No text may promise timbre there.**
2. ✅ **FIXED 2026-08-20 — BEND-LANE VIBRATO ALIASED IN BOUNCES on the hosted-AU path** (offline block 4096 → 512; Nyquist 5.86 → 46.875 Hz). ⚠️ Fact 3 below (CC 1 for sax vibrato) STILL STANDS on its own merits — the DLS sax’s internal 5.400 Hz vibrato is a different, and often better, sound than a bend lane. See m28-bug below for the measurement.
3. ⭐ **USE CC 1 FOR SAX VIBRATO.** The DLS sax has its own internal vibrato: depth linear in CC1 (`≈ 2.42 + 0.2996 × CC1` cents, ±40.5 ¢ at 127), fixed **5.400 Hz**, generated INSIDE AUSampler so it never crosses our bend lane and does not alias.
4. ✅ **Bend range CONFIRMED ±2.0155 semitones** — leg D's `bendRangeSemitones: 2` is right to 0.78 %. No correction factor.

That is **exactly 8× the bounce's 11.719 Hz**, re-derived independently. ⛔⛔ **THEREFORE THE USER HEARS ONE THING AND EXPORTS ANOTHER: a 5 Hz tremor is CLEAN live (Nyquist 46.9 Hz) and ALIASES in the bounce (Nyquist 5.86 Hz). That is the real bug, and it is now a confirmed monitor-vs-export divergence rather than a suspicion.** ⚠️ **`MIDIControllerRouting`'s block-sampling ceiling is a BOUNCE property and must NEVER be quoted for live playback.** The measuring probe was deleted deliberately — a gate that needs a running output device is a flake generator. **NEXT STEP, decisive and cheap: re-render the vibrato at `OfflineRenderer(maximumFrameCount: 512)`.** Aliases vanish ⇒ block size proven the lever, fix is one line (**recommend 512, matching the live buffer so bounce and monitor agree by construction**) — and it repairs EVERY hosted-AU automation export, not just the pad. Aliases persist ⇒ the AU smooths internally, no fix exists on our side, and CC 1 becomes the permanent vibrato route with the ceiling documented. ⚠️ Changing the block changes rendered bytes for existing projects carrying bend/CC automation — the m23-bv class. ⛔⛔⛔ **ESCALATED 2026-08-19 AT THE m28-p5 CLOSE — IT IS NOT JUST BEND. `CC 11` IS BLOCK-SAMPLED ON THE HOSTED-AU PATH TOO, MEASURED (not derived): the image/commanded ratio obeys `f/(f_s − f)` at four rates within 3 %.** Consequence: **§10.1's ENTIRE 4–8 Hz micro-tremor band is unusable on that path, not merely its top** — 52 % image at 4 Hz, and at **8 Hz the alias image is LOUDER than the commanded signal**. Holding an image 12 dB down needs **≤ 2.34 Hz**. P5 therefore SUPPRESSES tremor on `.soundBank`/`.audioUnit` with a warning naming our own 4096-frame block; drift (slow) lands everywhere. ⭐⭐ **THIS RAISES THE ITEM'S VALUE SHARPLY: the defect degrades EVERY fast controller automation on hosted-AU tracks in a bounce, not just vibrato, and a real feature is already suppressed because of it.** Route: `audio-dsp-engineer`, then `daw-architect` for the bytes call. ✅✅ **CLOSE-OUT 2026-08-20 — THE EXPERIMENT RAN FIRST AND CONFIRMED THE LEVER, THEN ONE LINE CHANGED.** `OfflineRenderer.swift` now defaults to `RenderBlockSize.offlineFrames` = **512** (new `Sources/DAWCore/RenderBlockSize.swift` is the single source of truth; the block↔modulation-rate coupling had been duplicated across three modules with no gate). ⭐⭐⭐ **THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS BELIEVABLE: the 4096 arm re-rendered the doc’s published table to the last digit** (47.55 / 35.41 / 19.22 / 3.18 ¢ commanded at 2 / 5.5 / 8 / 11 Hz; images 9.67 / 30.02 / 41.70 / 49.81 ¢; mean f0 290.686 Hz vs a published 290.687). At 512: depth **100.6 / 96.5 / 98.1 / 95.7 / 95.1 %** of commanded and **zero** in-band images; the 11.72 Hz case went from a static −17.9 ¢ detune (0.0 % depth) to 47.55 ¢ at 95.1 %. CC 11 the same — at 4096 the 11 Hz image was **15.6×** the commanded and the 8 Hz image **2.17×**; at 512 every ratio is ≤ **0.059**. ⭐⭐ **THE IMAGES DID NOT VANISH, THEY MOVED — to exactly `|93.75 − f|`, and they were FOUND there** (85.74 / 82.74 / 82.02 Hz in the local-maxima list, worst case ~7 ¢, two independent instruments — ZOH theory and the corrected demodulator — agreeing to ~1 %). A relocation to a PREDICTED place is far stronger evidence than an absence. **1024 was measured too and the data chose 512**: 1024 still counted 4 images (5.1–12.5 ¢ at 35–41 Hz) and left 4–12 % of depth on the floor. ✅ **P5’S SUPPRESSION IS LIFTED FOR THE PHYSIOLOGICAL BAND** — ceiling **2.34 Hz → 18.75 Hz**, so leg D’s 5.5 Hz vibrato and the whole 4–8 Hz micro-tremor band now land on the GM sax in a bounce. The machinery is RETAINED, not deleted (`tremorRateHz` is authorable to 20 Hz) and is now RATE-CONDITIONAL via `MIDIControllerRouting.modulationAliasesUnacceptably`. ⚠️ **A SECOND-ORDER HAZARD WAS FOUND AND CLOSED IN THE SAME PASS:** moving the block WITHOUT gating the suppression on rate would have printed “would need a rate at or below 18.75 Hz” and then suppressed a 4.565 Hz tremor anyway — a sentence contradicting its own action. ⭐ **MEASURED COST, not estimated** (8 hosted tracks, 120 s, bend lanes, `render()` only, 3 runs): 4096 = 0.449 s, 1024 = 0.514 s, **512 = 0.587 s → 1.31×, +0.138 s, still 204× realtime**. ⚠️ **RENDERED BYTES MOVED, as the item predicted — 4 test expectations updated with the reason recorded**: `AutomationFXParamTests` (22 → 186 automation steps; spread still exactly 0.0, max error 7.4e-09 — automation is now 8× finer on EVERY automated bounce), `SoundBankHostingTests` T5 (pinned to an EXPLICIT 4096 plus a new shipping-block arm: image/commanded 2.14 → 0.032), and both `ControllerLaneTests` warning tests (vibrato flipped suppressed→written; tremor now pins BOTH sides — 5.5 Hz written, 19.5 Hz suppressed). `BreathPadDeterminismTests` was re-pinned to the LITERAL `48000/4096` because that measurement is a fact about that block, not about the shipping one. New gate `RenderBlockSizeTests` asserts all three legs including RENDERED AUDIO (8 Hz arrives at 8 Hz, the 3.72 Hz in-band alias absent — asserted CONJUNCTIVELY, since prominence alone scores 28.56 on a flat trace). ⚠️ **THE CEILING, STATED PLAINLY: the image is MOVED AND ATTENUATED, NOT REMOVED** (~7 ¢ at ~82 Hz), and “512 matches the live buffer” is a DESIGN argument — the live buffer is device-dependent, so on a rig with a HAL buffer larger than 512 the bounce is now the FINER of the two. Full method + tables: `docs/research/measure-gm-sax-cc.md` §6–§7.

SF3 is structurally SF2 with **Vorbis-encoded sample data**, so the conversion is mechanical and one-way at import time and nothing downstream changes. ⚠️ **Until ② exists, our docs must stop implying general SoundFont support** — say `.sf2`/`.dls` plainly. **Ships with:** a control command + MCP tool surface unchanged (additive at most), and a test that a `.sf3` in a scan dir is REPORTED rather than swallowed. Route: `swift-app-engineer` for the discovery/report leg; `audio-dsp-engineer` if ② (Vorbis decode) is taken. **Blocks the m26-d bundle decision only in artifact choice, not in licence conclusion** — see the survey doc's correction section. ✅ **TIER ① DONE 2026-08-28 — the silence is fixed; the item stays OPEN for tier ②.** `scan()` now lists a `.sf3` with `format:"sf3"`, `supported:false`, and an actionable `unsupportedReason`; `SoundBankInfo` gained those two ADDITIVE fields and `instrument.listSoundBanks` / `instrument_list_sound_banks` carry them (no new command, no new tool — the wire pin is untouched; plugin bundle regenerated and grep-verified with a positive control). ⛔⛔ **LISTED IS NOT PLAYABLE, and that is guarded on purpose:** three independent gates reject by EXTENSION (`ProjectStore.validateSoundBank`, `Commands.parseSoundBankSource`, `SoundBankLibrary.importBank`) and **none of them reads the new field**, so labelling a format can never make it loadable by accident. The picker LISTS an unsupported bank (hiding it is the defect) but refuses to drill in and shows the reason in the inline alert — a silent no-op click would be this same bug in a different costume. ⚠️ **`bankInfo(at:)`'s old `ext == "sf2" ? "sf2" : "dls"` had to go first:** left alone it would have labelled the newly-listed `.sf3` as `"dls"`, i.e. traded an invisible bank for a loadable-looking lie. Gates: `Tests/DAWCoreTests/SoundBankUnsupportedFormatTests.swift` (9 tests, real files in a real temp scan dir, each absence positive-controlled) + 2 wire tests in `SoundBankCommandTests` + 2 model tests in `InstrumentPickerModelTests`. **Falsifiability PROVEN by planting two separate regressions** — reverting the discovery filter reddened 15 issues across both suites, removing the picker guard reddened 4 — not merely by the tests passing. ⛔ **STILL OPEN: tier ② (SF3→Vorbis decode at import), which needs a Vorbis decoder the tree does not link.**


## M32 — Sample flipping: turn a record into an instrument (seeded 2026-08-29 by the user)

The user's brief, verbatim: *"one more item to add support, unless it is already capable then
research and add skill that can write very rich music using sampling (Writing music using a
sample from an old record involves capturing, chopping, and reshaping a piece of audio into a
brand-new original track). Do a deep research and architect and implement what needs to be
implemented to support this"*

Research: `docs/research/sampling-flip-workflow.md` (`research-analyst`).

⭐⭐ **THE AUDIT'S HEADLINE, AND IT CUT THE MILESTONE ROUGHLY IN HALF: THE ENGINE IS ALREADY
MOSTLY CAPABLE. Every claim below was read from source by the main session on 2026-08-29, not
taken from an agent report.** The user's "unless it is already capable" clause is doing real
work here — three of the four things a sample flip needs are already shipped and merely
unreachable as a workflow.

✅ **ALREADY CAPABLE — DO NOT REBUILD:**

1. ⭐⭐ **THE KEYMAP PATH IS ALREADY VARISPEED.** `SamplerInstrument.swift:1371` —
   `voice.baseIncrement = exp2((Double(event.pitch) - Double(zone.rootPitch)) / 12.0)`. That is
   the source-frames-per-output-frame READ RATE, so playing a chop a fifth up reads the buffer
   faster *and* higher: **exactly MPC / SP-1200 / Recycle repitch semantics, which is what a
   flip wants by default.** `tuneCents` folds into the same rate (`:141`, `:587`,
   `exp2(cents/1200)` precomputed at init). ⭐ **CONSEQUENCE: v1 NEEDS NO NEW TIME-STRETCH
   MACHINERY** — and therefore never touches the per-slice elastic stretch this tree
   deliberately designed out (`AudioQuantize.swift:9`, *"the full-source-file stretch cache
   model forbids N per-span renders"*). ⚠️ **PATTERN TRAP THAT NEARLY HID THIS:**
   `grep 'pow(2'` returns **ZERO across all of `Sources/DAWEngine/`** — the tree uses `exp2`. A
   positive control proved the pattern was at fault, not an absence. "No `pow(2)` → no
   rate-based playback" would have been a confident wrong answer, and it would have bought a
   stretch engine we do not need.
2. **REGION PLAYBACK EXISTS.** `SamplerZone.startFrame`/`endFrame` (`Model.swift:1948-1954`) are
   SOURCE-FILE frames, resolved and defensively re-clamped at `SamplerInstrument.swift:534-535`,
   enforced at playback `:959`. Already on the MCP wire, and `server.ts:1194` documents this
   exact use case (*"Use with startFrame to excerpt one hit from a longer recording"*).
   ⭐ **So slice-to-keymap is GLUE, NOT ENGINE WORK.**
3. **GLOBAL MONO CHOKE EXISTS.** `voiceMode: .mono` + `monoPendingChoke` (`:365`, `:1148`,
   `:1333`) — every new note cuts the previous. **That IS the classic chopped-soul behaviour**,
   which demotes per-group choke from prerequisite to refinement.
4. **CHOP-TO-TIMELINE EXISTS.** `clip.quantizeAudio` at `strength: 0`; `AudioQuantize.swift:87`
   calls it *"the authentic Recycle/early-Logic slice behavior the spec cites"*, with span math
   at `:77-84` (slice i = source `[onsetᵢ, onsetᵢ₊₁)`, natural speed, never reads past the next
   onset).
5. **TRANSIENT DETECTION EXISTS.** `TransientAnalyzer.analyze` → `timeSeconds` + `strength`,
   spectral flux, refined to ~1.3 ms.

⛔⛔ **AND THE ONE HARD BLOCKER, WHICH GATES EVERYTHING ELSE AND FAILS SILENTLY.**
`SamplerInstrument.swift:479-511` loads every zone independently — **no URL keying, no dedup.**
Each zone opens the file and allocates a full private copy of the WHOLE file, per channel. For a
4-minute stereo 44.1 kHz vinyl rip (one copy = 80.7 MB): **8 zones → 0.63 GB · 16 → 1.26 GB ·
32 → 2.52 GB · 64 → 5.05 GB**, against **80.7 MB for any N with dedup**. Chopping is the one
workflow that makes many zones point at ONE long file, so this is precisely the axis a flip
loads. ⭐ It does not error — **it just allocates**, which is this tree's characteristic failure
mode wearing a new costume. (The only "shared" hit in the file is unrelated, `:288`; positive
control — "cache" DOES appear in `OfflineRenderer`/`PlaybackGraph`/`Metronome`, so the grep works
and the absence is real.)

⚠️⚠️ **TRAP FOR WHOEVER TAKES m32-f: `zone.group` IS NOT A CHOKE GROUP.**
`SamplerInstrument.swift:1171` — `if zone.group == lastFiredGroup { continue }  // group already
fired` — is an **exclusive-group / round-robin selector at NOTE-ON**, alongside
`seqLength`/`seqPosition` and `randMin`/`randMax`: only ONE zone per group fires per trigger.
**Choke is the opposite direction** — a new note killing an ALREADY-SOUNDING one. Reusing
`group` would silently break round-robin and alternate layers. A choke group must be a NEW
optional field.

⚠️ **TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RESEARCH DOC, BOTH MEASURED BY THE MAIN SESSION 2026-08-29 — one
in each direction, which is why both are recorded rather than just the flattering one.**
① **`clip.split` DOES EXIST** — `Commands.swift:272` (allCommands), `:3057` (dispatch), `:3067`
(unknown-key guard), `ProjectStore.swift:4184` (`splitClip(trackId:clipId:atBeat:)`).
⭐ **CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING PART: the research agent CAUGHT THIS
ITSELF ON REVIEW AND DISCLOSED IT IN PLACE.** Its first draft asserted the absence; it then
opened the 13 files its own grep had returned, found the claim false, corrected every affected

PAYING FOR, in a new costume: a grep returned 13 files and the conclusion "zero hits" was
written without opening one of them.** A hit count is not a reading.
⭐⭐ **AND THE CORRECTION PRODUCED THE MOST USEFUL STRUCTURAL FINDING IN THE REPORT — THE TWO
CHOP DESTINATIONS ARE ASYMMETRIC IN COST, AND TREATING THEM AS ONE TASK WOULD BOTH OVER-SCOPE
THE EASY HALF AND UNDER-SCOPE THE HARD ONE:**

in `Sources/`, positive-controlled with the same grep shape against `crossfade` (360 hits), so

a human DAW is the strongest point in it: **a human hears a click and undoes; an agent cannot
hear one before committing.** Folded into m32-b as a required property of every boundary, not a
separate item.

⭐⭐ **THE RESEARCH'S BEST STRUCTURAL FINDING, and it reorders the work: FOR AN AGENT,
DETECTION *IS* THE FLOOR.** A human eyeballs a waveform and clicks; manual placement is their
floor and detection an accelerant. An agent cannot "listen for the snare" — it can only call a
detector. So the usual priority inverts: **automatic chop detection is the floor, and manual
placement is what a HUMAN uses to override the AI's chops**, not what the agent uses to make
them. We already ship the detector (`clip.detectTransients`); what is missing is exposing the
SEGMENTS rather than only using them to snap audio invisibly.

capability Y", the load-bearing grep is the IMPORT LIST, not the symbol.**

**Chop-to-timeline is not even "reachable by composition" — it is ONE SHIPPED CALL:**

at frame *k*, so the concatenation IS the original waveform. **That is why the clip destination
needs no zero-crossing snapper, and why clicks are specifically a ZONE-destination problem:** a
slice played in isolation starts and ends at arbitrary sample values. (This supersedes the

tree's silent-success shape.** A `mode` picking a boundary SOURCE is a parameter; a `destination`
picking an output DOMAIN is a different verb.

  per-voice one-pole. Extending it is the cheap path; building a second filter architecture
  beside it is not. Revisit only if m32-c dogfooding produces evidence the one-pole is
  insufficient.

- [x] (m32-h) ✅ **DONE 2026-08-29 — the mono short read is fixed at both production sites.**
  `Sources/DAWEngine/AudioFileFullRead.swift` is now the one correct way to get N frames out of an
  `AVAudioFile`; `SamplerInstrument.init` and `ClipFadeBake.bakePiece` both route through it.
  Gate: `Tests/DAWEngineTests/AudioFileShortReadTests.swift` (5 tests, own non-`@MainActor` suite).
  ⛔⛔ **THREE CORRECTIONS TO WHAT THIS ITEM PRESCRIBED — all measured, and the first one matters
  most because the prescription as written makes the bug WORSE:**
  ⚠️ **PROVENANCE, STATED PLAINLY: the MAIN SESSION wrote that prescription when filing this item,
  from reasoning about an API it had not measured.** The probe I built measured the *defect*
  faithfully and I trusted it; I then guessed at the *remedy* in the same breath and wrote the
  guess in the same authoritative voice. ⭐⭐ **A VERIFIED DIAGNOSIS DOES NOT CONFER A VERIFIED
  CURE** — and the two sat in one sentence here, where the second inherited the first's
  credibility. The implementer measured it, refused it, and said so.
  ① **"Loop `read(into:)` until `frameLength` reaches `file.length`" DOES NOT WORK.** `read(into:)`
  does **not** append — it rewrites the buffer from frame 0 and RESETS `frameLength` to that call's
  own count (measured: 0→21 504, then 21 504→**546**, with `buffer[0]` now holding file frame
  21 504). `frameLength` can therefore never reach `file.length`; a third pass reads 0 and leaves
  `frameLength == 0`, which under `SamplerInstrument`'s `guard buffer.frameLength > 0` would SKIP
  every unaligned mono zone entirely. The correct shape is the one `BoundarySnapper` /
  `TransientAnalyzer` / `StretchRenderCache` already use: chunk-scratch + copy at a running offset,
  looping on **`framePosition`**, never on `frameLength`.
  ② **Reading AT end-of-file throws `Foundation._GenericObjCError.nilError`** — an exception with
  no message and no code, because the ObjC method returns NO without setting an NSError. (An
  over-ask with frames still remaining returns short quite happily; it is only the read AT the end
  that throws.) That is the real reason every correct loop here gates on `framePosition < length`.
  ③ **`read(into:frameCount:)` is affected too, and from a NON-ZERO `framePosition`** — truncation
  is to a 1024-aligned absolute FILE POSITION, not an aligned count (measured: start 1000 + 21 528
  = 22 528). That is what made `ClipFadeBake.bakePiece` a second, previously unlisted defect site.
  ⭐ **Only reads above ~12 000 frames truncate** (measured exact at 4 410…12 000, short at 15 434
  and 16 000), which is why so many small fixtures never showed it.
  ⭐⭐ **PINS MOVED: ZERO — and that is the finding, not a clean bill of health.** Instrumenting the
  helper across a full run shows **191 pre-existing mono, non-1024-aligned reads** in the suite,
  which pre-fix were losing **48 279 frames (~1 095 ms) of audio per run** — and not one existing
  assertion could see it. `SamplerLoopTests`' 66 150-frame mono fixture does load short today, but
  its A/B voice dies at source position ~57 330 (release ends ~2 400 frames after the note-off at
  60 000, increment 0.91875) and its loop points sit below 65 536, so the truncated region is never
  read; its `#expect(frameCount == 66_150)` reads through `TestSignals.readFile`, which already
  loops. The suite was blind here, so the new gate is the only thing holding this fixed.

  **The original report, kept verbatim below for its measurements — A SINGLE
  `AVAudioFile.read(into:)` SHORT-READS EVERY MONO FILE WHOSE FRAME COUNT IS NOT A MULTIPLE OF
  1024.** Found by `audio-dsp-engineer` while building
  m32-a's fixtures, **independently REPRODUCED BY THE MAIN SESSION 2026-08-29** with a standalone
  probe (`scratchpad/shortread-probe.swift`) — all five of its figures matched to the frame:

  | frames asked | mono got | lost | stereo got (positive control) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 22,050 | 21,504 | 546 | 22,050 ✅ |
  | 22,016 | 21,504 | 512 | 22,016 ✅ |
  | 44,100 | 44,032 | 68 | 44,100 ✅ |
  | 66,150 | 65,536 | 614 | 66,150 ✅ |
  | 88,200 | 88,064 | 136 | 88,200 ✅ |
  | 22,528 (1024-aligned) | 22,528 | **0** | 22,528 ✅ |

  ⭐ **STEREO READS FULLY AT EVERY ONE OF THOSE LENGTHS** — that is the positive control, and it
  is what proves the reader is at fault rather than the writer. Truncation is to a whole multiple
  of **1024 frames** (= 4096 bytes at mono float32); a second `read(into:)` returns the remainder.
  ⚠️ **CORRECTION TO THE FINDER'S OWN BOUND: they wrote "up to ~511 frames … up to 11.6 ms". The
  real bound is 1023 frames / 23.2 ms at 44.1 kHz** — my run measured **614** lost in one case,
  which already exceeds their figure. The mechanism was right; the bound was understated.
  ⛔ **`SamplerInstrument.init` issues exactly ONE read and then trusts `buffer.frameLength`, so
  every mono sample silently loses up to 23 ms off its tail.** It does not error — it just loads
  less. ⭐⭐ **THIS LANDS HARDEST ON EXACTLY THE M32 USE CASE: drum one-shots are usually MONO**,
  and a chopped one-shot losing its tail is a decay that stops early.
  ⚠️ **FIXING IT WILL MOVE EXISTING PINS:** `SamplerLoopTests`' 66,150-frame mono fixture loads as
  65,536 today, so the fix changes rendered audio for mono zones and needs its own byte-identity
  gate. **PREDATES m32-a and is untouched by it** — m32-a's fixtures use 22,528 frames (22 × 1024)
  specifically so that suite measures dedup and nothing else. Fix = loop `read(into:)` until
  `frameLength` reaches `file.length` (or the read stops advancing), not a single call.
  Route: `audio-dsp-engineer`.

⚠️⚠️ **BUILD ORDER — SERIALIZE m32-a → m32-d → m32-f.** All three touch the same four files
including a hot render loop, so running them concurrently invites both merge pain and a
build-contention false alarm. ⭐ **m32-b1 and m32-e are genuinely parallel with that chain** —
neither touches the sampler.
✅ **THE RESAMPLING LOOP (research §2.6, its last unmeasured floor item) ALREADY CLOSES ON THE
SHIPPED WIRE — verified, no item needed:** `render.bounce {path, fromBeat, durationSeconds,
excludeTrackIds}` returns `{path,…}`, `clip.addAudio {trackId, path, atBeat}` takes an arbitrary
path, and `render.stems` gives per-track prints. §2.6 is pure documentation for m32-c.
✅ **NOTHING IN M32 NEEDS FULL XCODE** — no entitlements, AUv3, or signing; only the ordinary
`/plugin update` + bundle regen once new MCP tools land. ⚠️ **`scripts/bundle.sh:93` still does
`rm -rf` IN PLACE on the path the live app runs from — make the user quit first.**

⚠️⚠️ **WIRE HYGIENE — AND THE MOVE-TOGETHER SET IS SIX SITES, NOT THREE. I UNDER-COUNTED IT BY
HALF, AND TWO OF THE THREE I MISSED FAIL SILENTLY.** New zone fields must be optional-nil so
existing projects decode unchanged, and these move together: `parseZoneFields`,
`samplerZoneSchema`, `SamplerZoneIdentityWireTests`, **plus** ⛔ **`merge(_:into:)` — a field it
does not know is SET via `zones` but NO-OPS via `zonePatches`**, ⛔⛔ **`SamplerZoneDocument` — a
field it does not know PARSES, PLAYS, AND THEN VANISHES ON SAVE/LOAD** (fields and `CodingKeys`
are enumerated explicitly; there is no synthesis to save you), and the MCP tool description.
⭐ **GATE = ONE FULL ROUND TRIP, because nothing smaller sees the silent two:** `zones` → save →
open → `describeSampler` → `zonePatches` → `describeSampler`.
⚠️ **ALSO MY ERROR, CORRECTED: merge-by-zone-id DOES exist.** `sampler.zonePatches` (m26-g,
`Commands.swift:9729-9765`) is described in-tree as *"the ONLY way to touch one zone of a
309-zone imported library without resending all 309."* A present `zones` array still replaces
wholesale; `zonePatches` is the merge path, and it is the post-chop tweak path the m32-c skill
must teach. ⭐ **Provenance of the error is the lesson: I took it from the wire-reference SKILL
SNAPSHOT loaded in my context, which predates m26-g. The file ON DISK is current
(`SKILL.md:252`).** *The record says X, the source says Y* — this time the stale record was my
own context.


## M33 — Dogfooding round 3: the sample-flip surface, used by someone who could not read the source (seeded 2026-08-29)

Log: `docs/dogfood/2026-08-29-session-2.md`. **16 findings (F1–F16) from ONE session** that made
a complete flip: 16 pads → 16 bars → −16.50 LUFS / −1.00 dBTP, 46.5 s, independently re-measured.

⭐⭐ **THE CONSTRAINT IS WHAT MADE THIS ROUND WORK, AND IT SHOULD BE STANDARD FROM NOW ON: the
dogfooding agent was FORBIDDEN TO READ PRODUCT SOURCE.** Every previous round was run by an agent
that could unstick itself by reading the implementation — which silently converts a documentation
defect into a non-event. Forbidding it turns each gap into a logged finding. Three of the sixteen
were defects in the skill *being tested*, which no unit test in this tree can reach, because the
artifact is prose.

⭐ **The round's meta-finding, in the agent's own words:** *"This surface's errors are its best
documentation, which is a compliment to the errors and a to-do list for the docs."* All five of
its hard blocks were recovered from an **error message**, never from a document.

✅ **ALREADY FIXED IN-SESSION (skill prose, `sample-flip/SKILL.md` 497 → 572 lines):** F1 (nested
`analysis.tempo.*`/`key.*`, no flat `bpm`) · F2 (`minSliceSeconds`, not `sensitivity`, is the
pad-count knob) · F3 (`count` ≠ pad count) · F5 (`pitch = baseNote + index`, 0-based) · F6
(`offset`/`limit` required to get zones) · F13 (project-vs-file measurement split) · F14 (the
`trackId: "master"` magic string) · F16 (which-reader-are-you before the delegation table) · plus
truthful wordings for F4 and F15. ⚠️ **NOT re-dogfooded — a doc fix is a hypothesis until someone
uses it.**

- [ ] (m33-a) 🐛 **F4 — a discarded head containing the downbeat warns about nothing.** MEASURED:
  a 0.333 s head holding the break's own downbeat produced **no warning**; the warning first fires
  around **0.714 s**. The skill promised such a head "can never vanish quietly" — **a promise the
  code does not keep.** ⭐ **The threshold is the bug, not the message**: a third of a second is a
  whole downbeat at any tempo a flip cares about. Prefer a RELATIVE test (head ≥ one slice width,
  or ≥ some fraction of the shortest pad) over the current absolute one. Doc side is already
  truthful; this closes the gap the other way. Route: `audio-dsp-engineer`.
- [ ] (m33-b) 🐛 **F6 — `instrument.describeSampler` omits the zone array unless you pass
  `offset`/`limit`, and nothing in the response marks the omission.** This is the tool whose stated
  purpose is handing back zone ids. **An empty-looking read is indistinguishable from a track with
  no zones** — this tree's characteristic silent-failure shape. Fix: default the window, or emit an
  explicit `zonesOmitted: true`. Route: `mcp-integration-engineer`.
- [ ] (m33-c) 🐛 **F12 — `audio.profileFile` DROPS `rmsDb`/`peakDb` for a digitally silent window
  instead of reporting silence.** On the one tool whose job is finding silence. ⚠️ **A defaulting
  read (`.get("rmsDb", 0)`) therefore reports 0 dB — FULL SCALE — for silence**, i.e. the loudest
  possible answer for the quietest possible input. Emit `-inf`/`-144` or a `silent: true` flag.
  Route: `audio-dsp-engineer`.
- [ ] (m33-d) 🐛 **F15 — `divisions: N` produces N−1 pads, and its warning describes a mode it is
  not in.** N cuts yield N spans and the head is discarded by default, so `divisions: 8` → 7 pads.
  The accompanying warning talks about "the detector" and "the first onset" **in a mode that runs
  no detector**. Either make `divisions: N` mean N pads, or say so in the refusal; fix the warning
  text either way. Route: `swift-app-engineer`.
- [ ] (m33-e) 😖 **F8 — `minSliceSeconds` merging keeps the EARLIEST onset of a cluster, not the
  STRONGEST.** Measured: a `strength 0.992` backbeat ended up buried 0.10 s inside a pad whose
  reported strength is 0.089. **The pad is mislabelled AND starts in the wrong place** — a chop
  that looks fine in the response and plays a ghost note. Prefer the strongest onset in a merged
  cluster. Route: `audio-dsp-engineer`.
- [ ] (m33-f) 😖 **F2 — `sensitivity` cannot reach the default `maxSlices: 32`.** On a clean break
  it bottoms out at 35 onsets, so the documented knob cannot satisfy the documented default. Either
  widen its range or stop presenting it as the pad-count control on the wire (the skill now points
  at `minSliceSeconds`). ⭐ **Its refusal message was singled out as one of the best on the
  surface — keep that.** Route: `mcp-integration-engineer`.
- [ ] (m33-g) 😖 **F7/F14 — the same object has three names across three surfaces.**
  `isMuted`/`muted`, `effects`/`fx`, `kind`/`name`, `isBypassed`/`bypassed` differ between
  `track.add`, `project.overview` and `fx.add`; the master chain is the undocumented magic string
  `trackId: "master"`, `fx.reorder` takes `index` not `toIndex`, `limiter.truePeak` defaults OFF,
  and `masterEffects` appears only in `project.snapshot`. ⚠️ **ADDITIVE ONLY — never rename a live
  field.** Add aliases and document; do not break the wire. Route: `mcp-integration-engineer`.
- [ ] (m33-h) 📄 **F10/F11/F13 — wire-reference doc gaps beyond the sample-flip skill.**
  `returnNotes: false` is documented as the cure for a documented context trap **and is rejected by
  name on the wire** (no doc says which layer it lives on); `audio.profileFile`'s **required**
  `windowSeconds` appears in no document and its promised DC/silence fields do not exist;

  re-verify each against a running build rather than against the source.
- [ ] (m33-i) 🔍 **F9 — `instrument_set_sampler_zones` is an MCP-side composite with no wire
  command.** Not a defect for MCP callers, but it means the MCP tool list and the wire command list
  are **not** in bijection, and a raw-wire caller following any doc that names it finds nothing.
  Already noted in the skill. Decide whether the two surfaces should be reconciled or the
  difference documented once, centrally. Route: `mcp-integration-engineer`.

⚠️ **Do NOT re-file the eight already fixed in-session (F1/F2-doc/F3/F5/F6-doc/F13/F14-doc/F16).**
m33-b/f/g above are the CODE halves of F6/F2/F14 — the doc halves are done.

### Round 3b — the SAME skill, re-dogfooded after the fixes (2026-08-29, `docs/dogfood/2026-08-29-session-3.md`)

⭐⭐ **THE FIXES WORKED, AND THE RE-RUN IS THE ONLY REASON WE KNOW.** A second agent, same
constraint (no product source), same break, and **not told what had been changed** — so
recurrence was the measurement rather than a leading question. It independently named §3a's
`headSeconds` paragraph *"the most load-bearing text in the document"* (it predicted its exact
0.333 s swallowed downbeat), plus §1's absent-`tempo.bpm` bullet and `audio_profile_file`'s
missing-field rule — **all three are round-3 repairs.** ⚠️ **But it also found that one of those
repairs was WRONG (F1 below), and a WALL in the skill's own step 8 that round 3 never reached.**

⭐⭐ **THE ROUND'S STRUCTURAL FINDING, and it restates this tree's characteristic failure mode
better than we had:** *"F2, F3b, F5, F6, F8 and F11 are all one shape — a call returning
something that looks like a valid answer. On this surface the refusals are outstanding; the
successes are what you have to distrust."*

⚠️⚠️ **CORRECTION LOGGED 2026-08-29, AND IT IS MINE: "DEEP AND DULL" WAS NEVER A DEFECT REPORT.**
The user's clarification, verbatim: *"I did not mean bad, it was just variance, but it was
pleasant… it was low frequencies which creates a nice effect, also 2nd version was good too and
FX was interesting and more pronounced."* **They were DESCRIBING the flip and they liked it. I
read a neutral description as a defect**, briefed the round-3b agent to treat it as one, wrote a
pass/fail brightness gate into the skill, and called it a "musical failure" here. ⭐⭐ **THE LAW:
A NON-MUSICIAN DESCRIBING WHAT THEY HEAR IS NOT FILING A BUG. Ask "did you like it?" before
acting; "deep" is a description, "wrong" is a verdict, and only the user can supply the second
one.** The skill's brightness section is now framed as AWARENESS, not a gate, and says plainly
that a darker flip is a legitimate aesthetic.

⭐ **What survives the correction, and it is still worth having:** the agent pitched NOTHING down
and still landed at `centroidHz` **534.9** vs the source's 1083.9 — a GM sub layer's harmonics
piling into the low-mid, with nobody intending it. It adjusted to **1169.1 Hz** and the user liked
**both**. So the value is not "brighter is better" — it is that **two different mechanisms can
drive a flip dark without the arranger noticing**, and measuring is how the darkness becomes a
choice rather than an accident.

✅ **FIXED IN THE SKILL IMMEDIATELY (all verified by me on a running build, not taken on report):**
F1 — **my own round-3 fix was wrong**: I wrote that `tonic`/`mode` are ABSENT when
`key.tonal: false`. Measured: `{tonal: false, tonic: "D", mode: "major", confidence: 0.209}` —
they are ALWAYS present and sometimes meaningless. ⭐ **And the two blocks behave OPPOSITELY —
`tempo` OMITS `bpm` when it detects nothing, `key` POPULATES a tonic — so "is the field there?"
cannot be the test for both.** · F5 — the reconstruction-clip length wall, with `clip_fit_to_content
{trackId, clipId}` as the cure (I reproduced both halves: a note at beat 20 on a 4-beat clip is
accepted with `warnings: []` and never sounds; fit grows it 4 → 21). · F8 — the overlap deletion.

- [x] (m33-j) ⛔🐛 **F8 — `clip.addAudio` SILENTLY DELETES ANY CLIP IT OVERLAPS. DATA LOSS, and
  the highest-priority item in this milestone.** REPRODUCED BY ME WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL: two
  imports at `atBeat: 0` on one audio track leave **ONE** clip, the first id dead, **both calls
  returning normal success with ids**; a third import at beat 40 leaves two, so the probe counts
  correctly and the deletion is specifically the overlap path. **No refusal, no warning, no trim.**
  ⭐ **It lands squarely on the resample loop we ship as central craft** — importing print after
  print onto one track is the documented workflow, and the obvious form of it destroys the
  previous import. Decide the policy (refuse / trim / layer to a new take lane) — but silence is
  not one of the three. Route: `swift-app-engineer`.
  ✅ **DONE 2026-08-29 — POLICY: REFUSE.** Re-reproduced through the real `clip.addAudio` router
  first (both adds `ok:true`, count 1, first id dead), and the probe ALSO found two facts the item
  did not have: a **partial** overlap silently TRIMMED the resident 4 beats → 2, and the identical

  drag-drop path) — see the two follow-up items below. `ProjectStore.importAudio` now asks the

  `ProjectError.clipImportWouldOverlap` (naming the resident + a free append beat) before any
  mutation; `overwrite: true` restores the trim/remove and returns
  `trimmedClipIDs`/`removedClipIDs`. ⭐ **Two existing conventions, no new invention:**
  `clip.moveManyToTrack`'s `clipsWouldOverlapOnDestination` (refuse a collision the VERB
  manufactured rather than pick which of the user's clips dies) and `vc.importVoiceModel`'s
  `overwrite` (refuse a destructive replace by default, honour it on request); the receipt is
  `clip.moveMany`'s. ⭐ **The deciding argument, worth keeping:** a move's footprint is a clip the
  caller can see, but an IMPORT's length comes from the file's duration at the current tempo — so
  `atBeat` alone never told the caller what it was about to cover, and a trim nobody could predict
  is not a trim anybody consented to. ⚠️ **The refusal's oracle is `resolvingOverlaps` ITSELF, not
