- ~~M4 (i) live mid-play send activation~~ **RESOLVED 2026-07-06** (diagnostic round 3, per the parked method: stderr instrumentation + node-connection dump + preallocated-atomic tap probes + the live `diag-send.mjs` repro). Root cause was NOT the send wiring: the connection dump immediately after the rewire resume showed the mid-play-added leg fully attached and connected (source mixer → gain(vol 0.5) → bus sum → chain host → bus mixer, 48 kHz/2ch throughout) and the gain node's tap FIRING — carrying peak 0.0. Two stacked mechanisms produced the "silent until stop/play" symptom, on ALL strips (bus A metered 0.0000 after the resume too — the old E2E's poll windows just never caught it): (1) **THE BUG** — the resume anchored `derivedBeats` on `outputNode.lastRenderTime`, which right after the stop→reset→start bounce still reports the PREVIOUS render session's sample clock (valid flags set, measured sample=98304) while the restarted session's clock begins again near 0; the `max()` clamp then froze the playhead at the resume beat for the ENTIRE prior session length (unbounded in a long session — why it read as "silent forever"), postponing the loop-wrap revival past every poll (predicted wrap +4.19 s vs observed +4.17 s, 36 ms match). (2) The repro material (7.5-beat sustained MIDI chord) has no note-on between the resume beat and the wrap, and no-chase is the settled v0 contract (`MIDIEventSchedule`, ARCHITECTURE.md), so the resumed schedule was legitimately silent until the wrap — "stop/play revives it" was simply a restart from beat 0 with fresh note-ons, not a topology repair. FIX (one flag): the rewire resume calls `startPlayers(…, renderClockTrusted: false)`, forcing the already-proven host-clock anchor branch (host time is monotonic across the bounce; players start on hostTime anchors in both branches, so nothing else changes). Live post-fix: MIDI pad send meters on B at +2.29 s (= the wrap, level exactly matching the stop/play reference, no transport command, A uninterrupted-then-revived per the restart contract); audio-clip send meters at +0.26 s with A continuously intact; bus E2E 19/19 (fx-poll window widened to cover the no-chase wrap, with comment); suite 920/117 green; app stderr clean.
- ~~Teardown crash: `project.new` after a played send/bus project~~ **RESOLVED 2026-07-12 (m13-a) — the crash class is dead BY CONSTRUCTION: once-rendered engines are never surgically detached; teardown-class changes discard and rebuild the whole engine.** Full arc, kept as the institutional record: **(1) 2026-07-06, discovery** during M4 (i) verification — build track→busA output + send→busB, `transport.play` ~1 s, `stop`, `project.new`, next `track.add` → SIGSEGV inside `-[AVAudioEngine connect:to:format:]` → `AVAudioEngineGraph::UpdateGraphAfterReconfig` → `swift_unknownObjectRelease` on a garbage pointer (`DAWApp-2026-07-06-051956.ips`; a sibling run crashed in a SwiftUI executor check, `…-051559.ips` — two surface stacks = heap corruption); the never-played variant did not crash. **(2) 2026-07-10, M9 crash-a fix** — diagnosis "detach against a stopped engine is unsafe"; mechanism = retire bin (`pendingDetachNodes` parked while stopped, `flushRetiredNodes()` after restart); live-verified 3× that day. **(3) 2026-07-12, FALSIFICATION** — the M13 audit (audit-m13.md B1) hit 3/3 staging sessions SIGSEGV'ing inside the fix's OWN flush path, and the m13-a C0 instrumented experiment named the mechanism with node-level evidence: after ONE engine stop→reset→start boundary, the FIRST flush-detach — of the routed source's strip mixer, with the engine RUNNING and `isRunning=true` logged at the call — is itself the faulting frame (instrumented addr `0x9ba885060 AVAudioMixerNode`, no survive line, `DAWApp-2026-07-12-104059.ips`; independently reproduced via `track.remove`, `…-104254.ips`). So "running at detach time" was NEVER sufficient: a node that RENDERED and then sat attached across a stop→reset→start boundary is already stale inside `AVAudioEngineGraph`'s internal node vector, and any later detach of it faults. The audit's "m12-f regression" suspicion was WRONG — same crash on the pre-m12-f binary; M9's 3× verification was heap-reuse luck. The C0 control leg (fresh-launch `project.new` ×20, engine never ran) survived 20/20, formally retiring the audit's session-3 "crash on first wire command" anomaly as mis-attribution (that shape cannot reach the crashing frame; plausible source = a foreign wire client, the documented 2026-07-11 staging-port anomaly). **(4) Resolution (m13-a; design docs/research/design-m13a-teardown-crash.md, supersedes fix-teardown-crash.md)** — retire-bin machinery deleted; announce-class reconcile on a once-rendered engine ABORTS before the first topology mutation and `AudioEngine.rebuildEngine(reason:)` discards the whole AVAudioEngine + PlaybackGraph and cold-builds from the model; `projectWillReplace()` forces the same rebuild unconditionally at project boundaries; `teardownDetach` detaches directly only against a running or never-run engine. Proven by the m13-a campaign: audit recipes verbatim + 12/12 played/unplayed × routed/plain matrix + 3× 41-track perf-c + 50-cycle soak (100 rebuilds, +0.4 MB RSS) + 20× fresh-launch — zero crashes, zero new .ips, m12-b offline anchors byte-identical, worst 41-track rebuild 143 ms.

- ~~Input device selection: pinned-device capture yields empty takes~~ **RESOLVED 2026-07-05.** Root cause was NOT the eager pin wedging the AUHAL (disproved by CLI repro: eager prepare + pin still delivers tap buffers). Two stacked bugs: (1) the same-device guard compared the pin target against the AUHAL's `CurrentDevice`, which on a fresh AVAudioEngine is the engine's PRIVATE AGGREGATE device — never equal to any raw hardware ID — so every pinned take (default uid included) performed a real device set; (2) that set makes AVFoundation post `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` on the capture engine ~65 ms after start with the engine still running and the tap still healthy, and the config-change handler treated it as fatal → `stopRecording()` finalized the writer before the first buffer, and the writer's post-finalize guard silently swallowed every later delivery (hence zero frames AND zero stderr). Fix: pin skips when the uid resolves to the current system default (`InputDevices.defaultInputDeviceID()`); config-change handler only ends the take when the capture engine actually stopped; two-phase `InputCapture.prepare()/start(writer:)` replaces the eager pin; 1.5 s first-buffer watchdog aborts loudly ("no audio arrived from input device …") instead of a silent empty take. Live E2E green: default-uid pin, ZoomAudioDevice pin (frames flowed), unpinned.

## M35 — `view.*`: let an agent SEE the app (seeded 2026-09-04 by the user)

Seeded while filming a session video. The user asked why the useful capture and
navigation verbs live only in the `debug.*` tier: *"if this is useful in
production, why not expose it in prod tools set … to end user who use AI to do
similar things"*. They approved building it, after the video ships.

**The gap, measured.** An agent over MCP can mutate the project but cannot look
at it. It can add a track; it cannot screenshot the app, open the piano roll on
a clip, frame what it wants to see, or open the panel it just changed. The four
capabilities already work as app-tier `debug.*` seams that are deliberately off
`CommandRouter.allCommands` and off MCP.

**Design is settled** — `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §"Key future decisions", first
entry: a typed app-layer seam (`ViewUISurface.swift`), copying the shipped
`PluginUIControlling` / `EditPasteControlling` pattern, so no AppKit enters
`DAWControl`. It names the schemas, the headless contract, the exact count pins
that move (211→215 Swift, 216→220 MCP), where in `allCommands` the
block must be inserted (after `plugin.listOpenUIs`, NOT the tail — 51
end-relative assertions), and the build order.

Found while shooting the session film, where every low chapter photographed a blank editor. Route: `swift-app-engineer`

## M36 — Three defects the film wave found in the product (seeded 2026-09-05)

Found while rebuilding the lesson films, each **reproduced with a control**, by
an agent that was trying to shoot a video rather than trying to break the app.
⭐ That is the point: dogfooding found these, not a test.

- [ ] (m36-a) ⛔⛔ **A SOUND-BANK INSTRUMENT RENDERS SILENT OFFLINE AFTER THE
  TRANSPORT HAS RUN — AND `render.bounce` STILL RETURNS `ok`.** Measured while
  filming Bach House: once the transport had run for a capture burst, **every**
  `soundBank` instrument in that app instance bounced to silence
  (`piano72.wav` came back at **−70 LUFS**), while the command reported success
  and simply **omitted the loudness report**. Re-issuing `track.setInstrument`
  did not revive it. ⚠️⚠️ **THIS IS THE HOUSE FAILURE MODE IN ITS PUREST FORM: a
  wrong answer that looks exactly like a right one.** An absent field is not an
  error, and every caller that does not check for it gets silence and a success.
  ⭐ **The fix has two halves and the second is the important one:** find the
  dropout, AND make a bounce that produced silence SAY SO — a render whose
  loudness report is missing must not return `ok`. GATE: bounce a soundBank
  instrument after a transport run and assert non-silence, with a
  pre-transport bounce as the positive control. Route: `audio-dsp-engineer`.
- [ ] (m36-b) **The GeneralUser GS path drops notes on dense material.**
  Identical pitches in bars 1 and 4 of BWV 846 rendered **14–64 dB apart** across
  three controlled renders of the same notes; shortening every note made it
  worse. ⚠️ **Consequence today: a sound-bank piano cannot be filmed**, which is
  why the Bach House rebuild uses the built-in `polySynth` for a piano piece.
  Route: `audio-dsp-engineer`. ⚠️ Check against m36-a first — they may share a
  cause, and fixing one may move the other.
- [ ] (m36-c) **`track.setVolume` clamps at 2.0 SILENTLY.** A request for 2.11
  stored 2.0 and rendered 3 dB under target with no warning. ⭐ The project
  already has the right shape for this — `fx.setParam` and
  `mixer.setMasterVolume` return a `warnings` array naming what was asked, what
  was stored, and the range, and the key is ABSENT when nothing was clamped.
  **Make `track.setVolume` do the same**; it is a small, additive fix.
  Route: `mcp-integration-engineer`.

## M38 — Polarity: the Ø button every mixer has and this one did not (2026-09-06)

- [x] (m38-a) ✅ **DONE 2026-09-06 — the gain insert gets a polarity (phase)
  invert.** `GainParams.invertPolarity: Bool`, default `false`, appended at spec
  slot 1 so `gainLinear` keeps automation slot 0. **`gainRange` was deliberately
  NOT widened to allow negatives**: `gainLinear: 0` already means silence, so a
  signed range makes 0 an awkward midpoint and fuses "turn it down" with "flip
  it" — a boolean is what the hardware does and what reads correctly as a
  toggle. Purely additive: a pre-m38-a project has no such key and decodes to
  `false` through the same clamping init `gainLinear` uses.
  ⭐ **NO new control command and NO new MCP tool** — effect params are a flat
  name/value surface, so it reaches the wire through the existing
  `fx.add` seeded-params path, `fx.setParam`, `fx.describe` and
  `project.snapshot` (pinned by two new tests in `FXCommandTests`; the wire
  count is unchanged at 215, `doc-count-drift` exit 0).
  ⭐ **RT: the sign is folded into the SAME smoothed coefficient the gain
  already ramps** (`GainEffect.signedTarget`), so a live flip walks +g → −g
  through zero on the existing ~5 ms declick — a brief dip, not a full-scale
  click — and `invertPolarity: false` is literally the same Float, unity skip
  included. No new smoothing framework, no allocation, no locks, no logging.
  ⭐⭐ **GATE = A NULL TEST SHOWN TO FAIL AS WELL AS PASS.** Two tracks, same
  transient-rich fixture (LCG noise bursts, NOT a sine), identical unity gain
  inserts, one boolean different: residual **exactly 0.0 → −∞ dBFS**. Control,
  same graph with the flag OFF: **−1.94 dBFS peak, +6.0206 dB over solo** — and
  planting `invert: false` into the null leg makes it fail at −1.94 dBFS, which
  is how we know the null is not vacuous.

## M37 — Cloud song generation: Lyria 3.5 and Eleven Music behind the existing provider protocol (seeded 2026-09-06 by the user)

The user's brief: *"include new AI feature to generate audio using ElevenLabs and
latest Google Lyra 3.5 model that is provided via API… That would be better than
using heavy ACE model that has worse quality. We may actually remove it
completely if google one is good."*

⭐ **The plumbing already exists.** `SongGenerating`
(`Sources/AIServices/Providers.swift:265`) is the contract, and there are already
two conforming clients — `ACEStepClient` (local sidecar) and `SunoClient`
(dormant cloud). A third and fourth are additive work, not architecture.

**Verified 2026-09-06 by web search, because both names needed checking and one
was wrong:**
- ⚠️ **It is Lyr*ia*, not Lyra.** "Lyra" is Google's low-bitrate *speech codec* —
  a different product entirely. **Lyria 3.5** is the music model, and it reached
  the **Gemini API in public preview on 2026-09-03** — two days before this item
  was written, and after my training data. Up to **3 minutes**, variable length,
  own-lyrics or generated, vocal-style and acoustic controls, image→track.
- **Eleven Music** is real and shipping: `POST /v1/music`, **3 s to 5 min**, up
  to **44.1 kHz**, MP3/PCM/µ-law/a-law/Opus. **Music v2** is the default in their
  UI; **v1 is still the API default during a transition**, so the model must be
  named explicitly rather than defaulted. **Paid subscribers only.**

⛔ **Do not re-open this as a refactor, a cleanup, or a side effect of adding a
cloud provider.** ACE-Step is the local/offline path and it is staying. A future
proposal to remove it needs a NEW ruling from the user, on new evidence — not a

The original argument, kept because it is the reasoning the ruling was made on:

Deleting ACE-Step is a one-way door and the case for it currently rests on an
untested claim. Three things argue against doing it as part of this work:

1. **Lyria 3.5 is in PUBLIC PREVIEW.** Preview APIs change shape and get
   deprecated. Deleting 56 GB of working local capability to depend on a
   two-day-old preview endpoint is the kind of trade that only looks good until
   it doesn't.
2. **ACE is the only OFFLINE path.** No network, no per-call cost, and nothing
   leaves the machine. For a DAW that is not a footnote: unreleased material,
   no connectivity, and per-generation billing are all real user situations.
3. **Rights and terms differ** between locally-generated and cloud-generated
   audio. That is the user's call to make with the terms in front of them, not
   an assumption to bury in a refactor.

⭐ **The milestone still ends in a MEASURED BAKE-OFF (m37-e)** — not to decide
whether ACE survives (it does), but to learn where each provider is actually
better, so the app can ROUTE to the right one instead of picking a winner.

> **The user's brief, 2026-09-19:** *"Should we try to build our own plugins for various instruments
> with various effects and parameters that can tune/modify sounds or produce entirely different
> synthetic/electronic/musical sounds… they should be easily controllable via MCP for AI Agent to
> manipulate it. It should be complete set that can bring music to the next level."*
>
> **User rulings the same night:** ship in **WAVES**, and **do not stop between them** — keep going.
> Modulation layer first, **and then creative effects in the following cycles** (*"Modulation is
> good, but then also in the next cycles Creative effects should be done as well"*). The user is
> asleep during the run and asked for **audio variants they can listen to afterwards**, with a
> handoff describing what landed and how to hear it.
>
> ⭐ **THE THESIS, and the reason this milestone exists rather than "host more plugins":** a
> third-party AU answers an agent with **opaque decimal parameter addresses and no semantics** — an
> AI can turn its knobs but cannot understand them. Plugins we build ourselves can publish named,
> unit-bearing, curve-declaring, documented parameters and preset catalogues a model can reason
> about. Every item below is scored on musical payoff **and** on whether it makes the surface more
> legible to an agent.

> ⚠️ **PREMISE CORRECTION, measured 2026-09-19 with a positive control.** The brief said our plugins

> **Measured cost base (2026-09-19, first-hand):** a new EFFECT kind = **6 exhaustive switch sites**
> (blast radius 29 files); a new INSTRUMENT kind = **8 switch sites** (blast radius 84). Those two
> numbers mean different things and must not be conflated. Full inventory, constraints and prior art:
> `docs/research/2026-09-19-plugin-program-inventory.md` — **read it before picking an M39 item.**

  boundary. The standard mitigation is interpolating the target coefficient across the block — or

  architect pass must price the interpolation explicitly; a design that budgets only "one `tan()`
  per quantum" has costed the wrong thing.** This is also why the richness pass (m39-g) was split

### ⭐⭐⭐ M39 CREATIVE EFFECTS — design frozen 2026-09-19

**Contract: `docs/design/2026-09-19-creative-effects.md` (§6–§7 frozen, §11 build plan, §12 nine test
gates). Read §2 and §3 BEFORE quoting a cost from §11 — the document carries a hard stop saying so.**

⛔⛔ **STOP: FOUR OF THE FIVE HIGHEST-PAYOFF CAPABILITIES IN THIS DOMAIN COST NOTHING TO BUILD.**
Do not open an item below without reading this block first. Building any of these as an effect kind
is wasted work on already-shipping mechanism:

- **Ducked reverb — ALREADY POSSIBLE, RENDERED AND MEASURED BY ME 2026-09-19.** Reverb on a bus +
  sidechained compressor keyed off the kick. Isolated-bus momentary-loudness swing went **0.5 LU
  (sidechain cleared) → 1.6 / 1.2 / 2.7 LU** as ducking deepened. ⚠️ **But in the FULL MIX it
  vanishes** — all variants ~1 LU, ducked no higher than control, because the reverb bus sits ~11 dB
  under the mix. **The feature works; the usage is what makes it audible.** Ships as preset + docs +
  a usage warning. ⛔ `duckAmount` was CUT from `HallReverbParams` on this measurement.
- **Filter sweep — ALREADY POSSIBLE** via `automation.addLane` on `eq.lowPassFreq` (no resonance).
- **Tremolo / auto-pan / free-Hz gater — ZERO COST BEYOND m39-e.** They fall out of the modulation
  layer's per-sample `.volume`/`.pan` takeover. Presets + demos only.
- **TEMPO-SYNCED TRANCE GATE — NO EFFECT KIND AT ALL.** It is `stepSequencer → .volume`.
  ⭐⭐ **The DJ research ranked it #1 TO BUILD; the honest answer is it is #1 TO DOCUMENT.** Same
  shape as M32, where the engine proved already capable and the milestone halved on measurement.
  ⚠️ Gated on m39-d + m39-c (sync).

⭐ **One correction in the OTHER direction — do not over-apply the above.** An **echo freeze is NOT
already possible**: `DelayParams.feedbackRange` is `0...0.95` and a freeze needs ≈1.0. Filed as
m39-k with its risk named (any test asserting the 0.95 clamp reddens, and `highCutHz` becomes
load-bearing at high feedback).

⚠️ **GATING.** Nothing tempo-synced ships before **m39-d** (live-vs-offline measured only at a
512-frame buffer; the non-512 case never measured) and **m39-c** (the sync resolver is hardwired to
`.delay` at five intake seams). **Gated:** synced trance gate, `.tapeDelay` synced mode, beat
repeat/stutter/half-time, granular freeze. **NOT gated:** everything in the top tier below — which
is why the top tier can proceed now. `.hallReverb` deliberately CUT `preDelaySync` to stay ungated.

⚠️ **DSP LAW from the primitive extraction: the denormal flush belongs to the CALLER, not to the
home.** `ChorusEffect` is feedback-free and carries no flushing, but **three of the extracted
`InterpolatedDelayLine`'s four new callers are feedback structures** (flanger, tape delay, FDN
recirculation). A home-side flush would tax every tap-only caller forever to protect callers that
must handle it anyway.

  1× → 4× on the demo fixture (19.77 dB at 2×), and **55.57 dB** on `ClipperTests` L1's own tone —
  two instruments, same verdict. Gate `scripts/gates/m39ac-clipper-physics.mjs`; three planted
  defects (factor forced to 1 / no anti-imaging filter / naive decimation) collapsed it to
  **0.00 / 1.30 / −0.00 dB**. ⚠️ **The oversampler was NEVER the hard part — the FIXTURE was.** The
  first spec drove the tone to −6.832 dBFS against a −6 dBFS ceiling, so the clipper applied gain and
  nothing else; all five variants rendered, all were byte-distinct, all were `audible=true`, and only
  the physics gate caught it. The gate now checks the clip DEPTH arithmetically before it scores.
  Latency is a **constant 32 samples at every factor** — a deliberate design invariance (see
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`), because a factor-dependent latency would stale the PDC plan that param
  edits never republish. Display name "Clipper" measured **35.677 pt** against the 85 pt budget,
  ✅ ~~Saturator v2~~ **SHIPPED as `m39-ad` 2026-09-20 — the second `Oversampler` caller, and the
  first time a SHIPPED kind gained a parameter.** `.saturator` gets `oversampling` (1/2/4),
  **APPENDED at slot 3** because slots 0–2 are in saved user automation lanes. Headline: the
  **ALIAS FLOOR drops 90.28 dB** 1× → 4× on the demo fixture (16.47 dB at 2×) and **69.76 dB** on
  `SaturatorOversamplingTests` L1's own tone — reproducing m39-ac's 91.05 dB through a different
  nonlinearity and the same filter. Gate `scripts/gates/m39ad-saturator-physics.mjs`; a planted
  sample-and-hold upsample collapsed it to **1.11 dB** and reddened the H3 invariance leg at
  **2.18 dB**, while the demo harness exited 0 with `audible=true` on all six variants.
  ⛔⛔ **THE DEFAULT IS 1, NOT THE CLIPPER'S 4, AND THE PRESERVATION IS MEASURED RATHER THAN
  ARGUED** (the "bend range stays 2.0" precedent): `scripts/gates/m39ad-saturator-default-bytes.mjs`
  pins THREE sha256s taken from the pre-m39-ad build — a no-effect CONTROL (so a pipeline change
  exits 3 "cannot score" instead of falsely blaming the effect), the untouched default, and a
  PARTIAL-MIX render. ⚠️ **That third pin exists because of a measured blind spot: `mix` defaults
  to 1, so the dry term is multiplied by zero and a REASSOCIATED blend passed the two-pin gate AND
  all 20 unit tests.** The pins were re-derived from an independently rebuilt `git worktree` of
  `a338854` and reproduced exactly, which is what makes a file hash usable as evidence.
  ⛔⛔ **`latencySamples` IS PARAMETER-DEPENDENT ON THIS KIND** (0 at factor 1, 32 at 2/4) — the
  thing m39-ac deliberately refused. Safe here, and ONLY here, because the factor moves on the MAIN
  ACTOR only (inside `applyParameters`, whose tail recomputes PDC — proven by
  `PDCWiringTests.saturatorOversamplingEditDrivesTheEngineRecompute`, which reddens on a planted
  render-thread read) and because the slot is **INERT to automation** — `AutomationTarget
  .valueRange` REFUSES a lane on it, the `delay.sync` precedent. The clipper's identically named
  param stays automatable and its latency stays constant; both asymmetries are pinned.
  ✅ ~~de-esser as a `.compressor` mode~~ **SHIPPED as `m39-ae` 2026-09-20 — the SECOND shipped
  kind to gain parameters, and the oldest one yet.** `.compressor` gets `detectorMode` (0 off /
  1 band-pass / 2 high-pass), `detectorFreqHz` and `detectorQ`, **APPENDED at slots 7/8/9** because
  0–5 are the original six and 6 is m23-ck's `mix`, all of them in saved user automation lanes.
  A de-esser is a compressor whose DETECTOR hears a filtered copy while the audio path stays the
  main input — so the filter hangs on the existing sidechain machinery and **NO new kind, and none
  of the EIGHT per-kind surfaces, was touched.** **This CLOSES `m23-cm`**, the 2026-08-04 pro-parity de-esser gap, whose predicted fix shape it matches exactly.
  ⭐ **HEADLINE, and it is stronger than a tolerance: non-sibilant material comes out
  SAMPLE-FOR-SAMPLE IDENTICAL** — 187 200 samples, bit for bit — while a broadband compressor at
  the same settings ducks it 3.23 dB. The detector never crosses threshold, the envelope snaps to
  exact 0, the gain is exactly 1.0, and the output IS the input.
  ⭐⭐ **THE LEG THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE REAL BUG IS THE DULL ONE** (the m39-ac/ad lesson, third
  time): a wideband de-esser applies ONE scalar, so it cannot move the BALANCE between two tones —
  measured drift **0.0013 dB**. A band-pass leaking into the AUDIO path is the single most likely
  way to build this wrong, and it would have stayed loud, stayed audible, kept ducking on
  sibilance, and passed every headline number. Gate `scripts/gates/m39ae-deesser-physics.mjs`, which
  also separates all three modes in a PREDICTED direction (high-pass ducks 5.22 dB harder than
  band-pass because a 2-pole high-pass has gain Q at its own corner), and positive-controls its own
  probe against a bin known to be EMPTY (the control reads −209 dB there).
  ⭐⭐ **TWO DEFECTS PLANTED AND BOTH CAUGHT, AND THE FIRST IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT:** (A) a **5 %**
  leak of the filtered detector signal into the AUDIO path — `render-variants.mjs` **EXITED 0 with
  `audible=true` on all four variants and plausible LUFS**, while the physics gate exited 1 with the
  balance drift at **0.423 dB against a 0.25 tolerance** and named the cause; (B) `.highPass`
  silently resolving to the band-pass section — caught by the mode-separation leg **at exactly
  0.00 dB**, plus the harness's own byte-distinctness check. Neither plant moved a headline number.
  ⛔⛔ **THE DEFAULT IS OFF AND THE PRESERVATION IS MEASURED** —
  `scripts/gates/m39ae-compressor-default-bytes.mjs` pins **SIX** sha256s from the pre-m39-ae build
  across TWO source families and TWO controls, and **all six reproduced exactly on a different
  binary after the feature landed.** ⚠️ **One of the six is SIDECHAIN-KEYED, and that is the pin
  that mattered:** this item restructured the detector's gather loop and a self-keyed-only fixture
  never executes its keyed limb. ⭐ **The `Biquad` moved to `Primitives/` as the `Oversampler`
  precedent requires** (second caller = extract), proven by re-pinning the EXISTING `ringmod` demo
  set — a fixture that cannot have been shaped to pass — plus a unit test against a hand-copy of the
  original expressions. **Positive-controlled: 1e-25 → 1e-20 in the flush reddened all three
  ring-mod variants while the control held, and left the compressor gate green.**
  ⚠️ **A CRASH WAS FOUND BY A TEST WRITING ITSELF:** `detectorMode(at:)` guarded only `isFinite`,
  and `Int(1e300)` **traps** — a render-thread crash reachable through a field-by-field automation
  poke, which bypasses the clamping init. `.clamped(to:)` now comes BEFORE the conversion, the
  `ClipperParams.mode(at:)` shape. ⛔ **Latency stays a literal 0 at every setting**, so unlike
  m39-ad no automation lane is refused — the refusal there was about latency, not about discreteness.
  Verdict table 131 → 134 (0 yes / 2 warned / 1 refused — the first kind to add more `warned` than
  `yes`). Demo sets `deesser.json` (physics), `deesser-listening.json` (4 variants on `thresholdDb`),
  `deesser-bytes.json` (the pin fixture).
  ⛔⛔ **THE LISTENING FIXTURE DEMONSTRATED THE OPPOSITE OF ITS OWN TEXT, AND ONLY A MEASUREMENT
  OF THE FIXTURE ITSELF COULD SEE IT.** The first cut used a sawtooth voice; inside the detector
  band the sibilant blip was only **5.5 dB** above the sustained notes, so every threshold that
  caught the blip also ducked the vowels (**1.5 dB** at `medium`, **6.2 dB** at `strong`) while the
  prose claimed they were untouched — and all four variants rendered, measured `audible=true`, and
  came out byte-distinct. Retuned to a triangle voice with the blip on its own fundamental in the
  band: separation **33.1 dB**, vowel GR **0.03 dB** at `medium`, and the whole first note
  (**42 000 samples**) bit-identical to a no-compressor render, against the plain compressor at the
  SAME threshold ducking those notes **5.0 dB**. ⭐ **LAW: a listening fixture's load-bearing number
  is the SEPARATION between what the effect targets and what it must leave alone — measure it
  BEFORE choosing the axis; no gate, harness or ear check in this tree can substitute.**
  ⚠️ The control was also re-pointed to the de-essed middle variant's threshold so the A/B turns on
  `detectorMode` alone; at its old −24 it ducked nothing and the "before" half of the demo was inert.
  Remaining in this bullet:
  dynamic EQ (⚠️ **ADOPT m23-cl**).
  ⛔ **DEFERRED to their own spikes, do not let one absorb another:** beat repeat / tape stop /
  backspin / half-time (need a capture ring buffer + the frozen-but-unbuilt position-delivery API),
  granular freeze (a grain scheduler is a different primitive again), shimmer/pitch shifter.
  Full per-item contracts, weights and rejected alternatives: the design doc §11.
